sentences.zh: 【晉紀三十七】 起屠維作噩，盡上章鬮茂，凡二年。

translations.literal: [Jin Records 37] From Tuyu Zuo'e through Shangzhang Jiumao; two years in all.
translations.idiomatic: [Jin Records 37] From Tuyu Zuo'e through Shangzhang Jiumao—two years in all.

sentences.zh: 安皇帝庚義熙五年（

translations.literal: Emperor An, the fifth year of Yixi (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor An, the fifth year of Yixi (

sentences.zh: 己酉，公元四零九年）

translations.literal: jiyou, AD 409)
translations.idiomatic: jiyou, AD 409)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，庚寅朔，南燕主超朝會群臣，歎太樂不備，議掠晉人以補伎。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on gengyin the new moon, the ruler of Southern Yan, Murong Chao, held court with his ministers, lamented that the imperial music corps was incomplete, and discussed raiding Jin subjects to supply performers.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on the gengyin new moon, Southern Yan's ruler Murong Chao convened his ministers, lamented that the imperial music establishment was incomplete, and proposed raiding Jin territory to seize people to train as performers.

sentences.zh: 領軍將軍韓言卓曰：「先帝以舊京傾覆，戢翼三齊。

translations.literal: General of the Household Guards Han Yanzhuo said: "The late emperor, when the old capital fell, folded his wings in the Three Qis.
translations.idiomatic: General of the Household Guards Han Yanzhuo said, "When the old capital fell, the late emperor folded his wings in the Three Qis.

sentences.zh: 陛下不養士息民，以伺魏釁，恢復先業，而更侵掠南鄰以廣仇敵，可乎！」

translations.literal: Your Majesty does not nurture scholars and give the people rest, to watch for an opening against Wei and restore the former enterprise, but instead raids the southern neighbor to multiply enemies—how can this be right!"
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty does not nurture talent and let the people recover, watching for a chance against Wei to restore our forefathers' work, yet you would raid the southern neighbor and multiply our enemies—how can that be right?"

sentences.zh: 超曰：「我計已定，不與卿言。」

translations.literal: Chao said: "My plan is already set; I will not discuss it with you."
translations.idiomatic: Chao said, "My mind is made up. I have nothing more to say to you."

sentences.zh: 辛卯，大赦。

translations.literal: On xinmao, a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao, a general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，以劉毅為衛將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: On gengxu, Liu Yi was appointed General of the Guards and given the Grand Marshal's Staff with Protocol Equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu, Liu Yi was made General of the Guards with a grand marshal's staff and protocol equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 毅愛才好士，當世名流莫不輻湊，獨揚州主簿吳郡張邵不往。

translations.literal: Yi loved talent and honored scholars; not one famous man of the age failed to gather around him—only Zhang Shao of Wu commandery, Registrar of Yang province, did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Yi loved talent and honored men of learning, and every notable of the age flocked to him—only Zhang Shao of Wu, registrar of Yang province, stayed away.

sentences.zh: 或問之，邵曰：「主公命世人傑，何煩多問！」

translations.literal: When someone asked him about it, Shao said: "Our lord is a hero of the age—why trouble oneself with so many questions!"
translations.idiomatic: When someone asked why, Shao said, "Our lord is a hero of the age—why pester him with questions?"

sentences.zh: 秦王興遣其弟平北將軍沖、征虜將軍狄伯支等帥騎四萬擊夏王勃勃。

translations.literal: King Xing of Qin sent his younger brother, General Who Pacifies the North Yao Chong, General Who Conquers Barbarians Di Bozhi, and others at the head of forty thousand horsemen to attack the Xia king Helian Bobo.
translations.idiomatic: King Xing of Qin sent his younger brother Yao Chong, General Who Pacifies the North, and Di Bozhi, General Who Conquers Barbarians, with forty thousand cavalry to attack the Xia king Helian Bobo.

sentences.zh: 衝至嶺北，謀還襲長安，伯支不從而止；

translations.literal: Chong reached north of the mountains and plotted to turn back and strike Chang'an; Bozhi would not follow, and Chong stopped;
translations.idiomatic: Chong reached north of the mountains and plotted to turn back and strike Chang'an; Bozhi refused to go along, so Chong abandoned the plan;

sentences.zh: 因鴆殺伯支以滅口。

translations.literal: he then poisoned Bozhi to silence him.
translations.idiomatic: then he poisoned Bozhi to silence him.

sentences.zh: 秦王興遣使冊拜譙縱為大都督、相國、蜀王，加九錫，承製封拜，悉如王者之儀。

translations.literal: King Xing of Qin sent envoys to invest Qiao Zong as Grand Commander-in-Chief, Chancellor, and King of Shu, with the Nine Bestowals, authority to issue edicts and grant titles—all the ceremonies of a king.
translations.idiomatic: King Xing of Qin sent envoys to invest Qiao Zong as Grand Commander-in-Chief, Chancellor, and King of Shu, with the Nine Bestowals and authority to issue edicts and grant titles, with all the ceremony due a king.

sentences.zh: 二月，南燕將慕容興宗、斛谷提、公孫歸等帥騎寇宿豫，拔之，大掠而去，簡男女二千五百付太樂教之。

translations.literal: In the second month, the Southern Yan generals Murong Xingzong, Hugu Ti, Gongsun Gui, and others led cavalry to raid Suyu, took it, plundered heavily and withdrew, and selected twenty-five hundred men and women to hand over to the imperial music office for training.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, Southern Yan generals Murong Xingzong, Hugu Ti, and Gongsun Gui led cavalry against Suyu, captured it, plundered the region, and withdrew with twenty-five hundred men and women selected for the imperial music office to train.

sentences.zh: 歸，五樓之兄也。

translations.literal: Gui was the elder brother of Wulou.
translations.idiomatic: Gui was the elder brother of Wulou.

sentences.zh: 是時，五樓為侍中、尚書、領左衛將軍，專總朝政，宗親並居顯要，王公內外無不憚之。

translations.literal: At this time Wulou was Attendant-in-Ordinary, Master of Writing, and Commander of the Left Guards, monopolizing court affairs; kinsmen all held prominent posts, and none within or without the royal house did not fear him.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Wulou was attendant-in-ordinary, master of writing, and commander of the Left Guards, monopolizing court affairs; his kinsmen all held high office, and everyone inside and outside the royal house feared him.

sentences.zh: 南燕主超論宿豫之功，封斛谷提等並為郡、縣公。

translations.literal: The Southern Yan ruler Chao discussed the merit of the Suyu campaign and enfeoffed Hugu Ti and the others as dukes of commanderies and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chao reviewed the Suyu campaign and enfeoffed Hugu Ti and the others as commandery and county dukes.

sentences.zh: 桂林王鎮諫曰：「此數人者，勤民頓兵，為國結怨，何功而封？」

translations.literal: Prince of Guilin Zhen remonstrated, saying: "These men have wearied the people and exhausted the army, heaping resentment on the state—what merit warrants enfeoffment?"
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Guilin Murong Zhen remonstrated, "These men have exhausted the people and the army and earned the state's enmity—what merit warrants enfeoffment?"

sentences.zh: 超怒，不答。

translations.literal: Chao was angry and made no reply.
translations.idiomatic: Chao was furious and gave no answer.

sentences.zh: 尚書都令史王儼諂事五樓，比歲屢遷，官至左丞。

translations.literal: Wang Yan, Chief Clerk of the Masters of Writing, flattered Wulou; year after year he was promoted until he reached the post of Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan, chief clerk of the Masters of Writing, curried favor with Wulou and was promoted year after year until he became left vice director.

sentences.zh: 國人為之語曰：「欲得侯，事五樓。」

translations.literal: The people made a saying: "If you want to be enfeoffed, serve Wulou."
translations.idiomatic: People said, "Want a marquisate? Serve Wulou."

sentences.zh: 超又遣公孫歸等寇濟南，俘男女千餘人而去。

translations.literal: Chao again sent Gongsun Gui and others to raid Jinan, seized more than a thousand men and women, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Chao again sent Gongsun Gui and others against Jinan; they seized more than a thousand men and women and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 自彭城以南，民皆堡聚以自固。

translations.literal: From Pengcheng southward, the people all fortified stockades to protect themselves.
translations.idiomatic: From Pengcheng southward, the people fortified stockades everywhere for self-defense.

sentences.zh: 詔并州刺史劉道憐鎮淮陰以備之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Liu Daolian, Inspector of Bing province, to garrison Huaiyin on guard against them.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Liu Daolian, inspector of Bing province, to garrison Huaiyin against them.

sentences.zh: 乞伏熾磐入見秦太原公懿於上邽，彭奚念乘虛伐之。

translations.literal: Qifu Chipan went in to see the Qin Prince of Taiyuan, Yao Yi, at Shanggui; Peng Xinian seized the moment of his absence to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Qifu Chipan went to Shanggui to see Yao Yi, Prince of Taiyuan of Qin; Peng Xinian attacked his territory while he was away.

sentences.zh: 熾磐聞之，怒，不告懿而歸，擊奚念，破之，遂圍枹罕。

translations.literal: Chipan heard of it, was enraged, returned without informing Yi, struck Xinian and defeated him, then besieged Fuhan.
translations.idiomatic: When Chipan heard, he was furious; without telling Yi, he marched home, defeated Xinian, and besieged Fuhan.

sentences.zh: 乞伏乾歸從秦王興如平涼；

translations.literal: Qifu Qian'gui had followed King Xing of Qin to Pingliang;
translations.idiomatic: Qifu Qian'gui had followed King Xing of Qin to Pingliang;

sentences.zh: 熾磐克枹罕，遣人告乾歸，乾歸逃還苑川。

translations.literal: Chipan took Fuhan and sent word to Qian'gui; Qian'gui fled back to Yuanchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Chipan captured Fuhan and sent word to Qian'gui, who fled back to Yuanchuan.

sentences.zh: 馮翊人劉厥聚眾數千，據萬年作亂，秦太子泓遣鎮軍將軍彭白狼帥東宮禁兵討之，斬厥，赦其餘黨。

translations.literal: Liu Jue of Fengyi gathered several thousand men, seized Wannian and rebelled; the Qin crown prince Hong sent General Who Pacifies the Army Peng Bailang at the head of the Eastern Palace guard to suppress him, beheaded Jue, and pardoned the rest of his faction.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jue of Fengyi raised several thousand men, seized Wannian, and rebelled; Crown Prince Hong of Qin sent Peng Bailang, General Who Pacifies the Army, with the Eastern Palace guard to suppress him, beheaded Jue, and pardoned the rest of his followers.

sentences.zh: 諸將請露布，表言廣其首級。

translations.literal: The generals asked to issue a victory bulletin and memorialize that the display of heads be enlarged.
translations.idiomatic: The generals asked to issue a victory bulletin and memorialize that more severed heads be displayed.

sentences.zh: 泓不許，曰：「主上委吾後事，不能式遏寇逆，當責躬請罪，尚敢矜誕自為功乎！」

translations.literal: Hong would not allow it, saying: "The sovereign entrusted me with his rear affairs; I could not check the rebels—I ought to blame myself and beg punishment. How dare I boast and claim merit!"
translations.idiomatic: Hong refused, saying, "The sovereign entrusted the rear to me, and I failed to stop the rebels—I should take the blame and beg punishment. How dare I boast and claim merit!"

sentences.zh: 秦王興自平涼如朝那，聞姚沖之謀，賜沖死。

translations.literal: King Xing of Qin went from Pingliang to Chaona and, hearing of Yao Chong's plot, ordered Chong to die.
translations.idiomatic: King Xing of Qin went from Pingliang to Chaona; when he learned of Yao Chong's plot, he ordered Chong to take his own life.

sentences.zh: 三月，劉裕抗表伐南燕，朝議皆以為不可，惟左僕射孟昶、車騎司馬謝裕、參軍臧熹以為必克，勸裕行。

translations.literal: In the third month, Liu Yu submitted a memorial resisting court opinion to campaign against Southern Yan; the court debate all held it impossible—only Left Vice Director Meng Chang, Chief of Staff to the Chariots and Cavalry Xie Yu, and Army Aide Zang Xi held that victory was certain and urged Yu to go.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, Liu Yu memorialized the throne proposing a campaign against Southern Yan; court opinion overwhelmingly opposed it, but Left Vice Director Meng Chang, Chief of Staff to the Chariots and Cavalry Xie Yu, and army aide Zang Xi were convinced of victory and urged him to go.

sentences.zh: 裕以昶監中軍留府事。

translations.literal: Yu made Chang oversee central army affairs and remain to manage the headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Yu left Chang in charge of central army affairs at headquarters.

sentences.zh: 謝裕，安之兄孫也。

translations.literal: Xie Yu was the grandson of Xie Yu the elder's elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Yu was a grandson of Xie An's elder brother.

sentences.zh: 初，苻氏之敗也，王猛之孫鎮惡來奔，以為臨澧令。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Fu clan fell, Wang Zhen'e, grandson of Wang Meng, came as a refugee and was made magistrate of Linli.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the Fu clan fell, Wang Zhen'e, grandson of Wang Meng, came as a refugee and was appointed magistrate of Linli.

sentences.zh: 鎮惡騎乘非長，關弓甚弱，而有謀略，善果斷，喜論軍國大事。

translations.literal: Zhen'e was not skilled at riding, drew the bow very weakly, yet had stratagems, was good at decisive action, and delighted in discussing military and state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen'e was a poor horseman and a weak archer, but he was resourceful, decisive, and loved to discuss military and state affairs.

sentences.zh: 或薦鎮惡於劉裕，裕與語，說之，因留宿。

translations.literal: Someone recommended Zhen'e to Liu Yu; Yu conversed with him, was pleased, and kept him overnight.
translations.idiomatic: Someone recommended Zhen'e to Liu Yu; Yu talked with him, was delighted, and kept him overnight.

sentences.zh: 明旦，謂參佐曰：「吾聞將門有將，鎮惡信然。」

translations.literal: The next morning he told his staff: "I have heard that general's households produce generals—Zhen'e is truly so."
translations.idiomatic: The next morning he told his staff, "They say general's households breed generals—Zhen'e proves it."

sentences.zh: 即以為中軍參軍。

translations.literal: He immediately made him an aide on the central army staff.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately appointed him an aide on the central army staff.

sentences.zh: 恆山崩。

translations.literal: Mount Heng collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Mount Heng collapsed.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，乞伏乾歸如枹罕，留世子熾磐鎮之，收其眾得二萬，徙都度堅山。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, Qifu Qian'gui went to Fuhan, left the heir Chipan to garrison it, gathered its forces to twenty thousand, and moved the capital to Dujianshan.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, Qifu Qian'gui went to Fuhan, left his heir Chipan to garrison it, gathered twenty thousand troops from the region, and moved the capital to Dujianshan.

sentences.zh: 雷震魏天安殿東序。

translations.literal: Thunder struck the eastern gallery of the Wei dynasty's Tian'an Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Lightning struck the eastern gallery of the Wei dynasty's Hall of Heavenly Peace.

sentences.zh: 魏主珪惡之，命左校以沖車攻東、西序，皆毀之。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler Gui took it as ill omen and ordered the Left Construction Office to attack the eastern and western galleries with battering rams and destroy them all.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gui of Wei took it as an ill omen and ordered the construction office to batter and destroy both the eastern and western galleries.

sentences.zh: 初，珪服寒食散，久之，藥發，性多躁擾，忿怒無常，至是浸劇。

translations.literal: Earlier, Gui had taken cold-food powder; after long use the drug flared up, his nature grew restless and agitated, and his anger was ungovernable—by now it grew worse.
translations.idiomatic: Gui had long taken cold-food powder; over time the drug's effects worsened, leaving him restless, irritable, and prone to fits of rage—and now it grew worse.

sentences.zh: 又災異數見，占者多言當有急變生肘腋。

translations.literal: Omens and prodigies also appeared repeatedly; diviners mostly said sudden crisis would arise at his very side.
translations.idiomatic: Omens and portents multiplied, and diviners mostly warned of sudden crisis at his elbow.

sentences.zh: 珪憂懣不安，或數日不食，或達旦不寐，追計平生成敗得失，獨語不止。

translations.literal: Gui was anxious and uneasy, sometimes going days without food or staying awake till dawn, reckoning the gains and losses of a lifetime, talking to himself without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Gui grew anxious and distraught, sometimes going days without eating or staying awake till dawn, reckoning life's gains and losses and muttering to himself without end.

sentences.zh: 疑群臣左右皆不可信，每百官奏事至前，追記其舊惡，輒殺之；

translations.literal: He suspected that ministers and attendants alike were untrustworthy; whenever an official came to report business, he would recall some old offense and kill him on the spot;
translations.idiomatic: He suspected that none of his ministers or attendants could be trusted; whenever an official came to report, he would recall some old offense and kill him on the spot;

sentences.zh: 其餘或顏色變動，或鼻息不調，或步趨失節，或言辭差繆，皆以為懷惡在心，發形於外，往往以手擊殺之，死者皆陳天安殿前。

translations.literal: the rest, if their expression shifted, their breathing was irregular, their gait faltered, or their words slipped, he took as malice in the heart showing in the body—often he beat them to death with his own hands, and the dead were laid out before Tian'an Hall.
translations.idiomatic: others he killed for a change of expression, irregular breathing, an unsteady step, or a slip of the tongue, convinced that malice in the heart had betrayed itself in the body; he often beat them to death with his own hands, and the corpses were laid out before the Hall of Heavenly Peace.

sentences.zh: 朝廷人不自保，百官苟免，莫相督攝；

translations.literal: No one at court could protect himself; officials merely sought to escape blame and none supervised one another;
translations.idiomatic: No one at court felt safe; officials merely tried to survive and no one supervised anyone else;

sentences.zh: 盜賊公行，里巷之間，人為希少。

translations.literal: bandits walked openly, and people in the lanes were few.
translations.idiomatic: bandits roamed openly, and the streets were nearly empty.

sentences.zh: 珪亦知之，曰：「朕故縱之使然，待過災年，當更清治之耳。」

translations.literal: Gui knew this too and said: "I deliberately let it go on; after the disaster years pass, I shall clean it up again."
translations.idiomatic: Gui knew this too and said, "I let it happen on purpose; after the bad years pass, I will clean it up again."

sentences.zh: 是時，群臣畏罪，多不敢求親近，唯著作郎崔浩恭勤不懈，或終日不歸。

translations.literal: At this time the ministers, fearing guilt, mostly dared not seek proximity—only Editorial Director Cui Hao was respectful and diligent without slackening, sometimes not returning home all day.
translations.idiomatic: At this time most ministers, fearing for their lives, dared not stay near him—only Cui Hao, editorial director, served with unwavering diligence, sometimes not going home for a whole day.

sentences.zh: 浩，吏部尚書宏之子也。

translations.literal: Hao was the son of Minister of the Civil Service Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Hao was the son of Minister of the Civil Service Cui Hong.

sentences.zh: 宏未嘗忤旨，亦不諂諛，故宏父子獨不被遣。

translations.literal: Hong had never defied an order, yet never flattered either; therefore father and son alone were not sent away.
translations.idiomatic: Hong had never defied an order, yet never flattered either; father and son alone were not driven away.

sentences.zh: 夏王勃勃帥騎二萬攻秦，掠取平涼雜胡七千餘戶，進屯依力川。

translations.literal: The Xia king Bobo led twenty thousand horsemen to attack Qin, carried off more than seven thousand households of mixed Hu from Pingliang, and advanced to camp on the Yili River.
translations.idiomatic: Xia king Helian Bobo led twenty thousand cavalry against Qin, seized more than seven thousand mixed Hu households from Pingliang, and encamped on the Yili River.

sentences.zh: 己巳，劉裕發建康，帥舟師自淮入泗。

translations.literal: On jisi, Liu Yu set out from Jiankang and led a fleet from the Huai into the Si.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi, Liu Yu left Jiankang and led his fleet from the Huai into the Si.

sentences.zh: 五月，至下邳，留船艦、輜重，步進至琅邪。

translations.literal: In the fifth month he reached Xiapi, left ships and baggage train, and marched on foot to Langye.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he reached Xiapi, left his ships and baggage, and marched on foot to Langye.

sentences.zh: 所過皆築城，留兵守之。

translations.literal: Wherever he passed he built fortifications and left troops to garrison them.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he passed he built fortifications and left troops to hold them.

sentences.zh: 或謂裕曰：「燕人若塞大峴之險，或堅壁清野，大軍深入，不唯無功，將不能自歸，奈何？」

translations.literal: Someone said to Yu: "If the Yan men block the Da'xian pass or clear the countryside behind strong walls, when the great army penetrates deep, not only will there be no success—you may not be able to return. What then?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone said to Yu, "If the Yan block the Da'xian pass or clear the countryside, your army will penetrate deep with no gain—and may not get home again. What then?"

sentences.zh: 裕曰：「吾慮之熟矣。

translations.literal: Yu said: "I have thought this through thoroughly.
translations.idiomatic: Yu said, "I have thought this through.

sentences.zh: 鮮卑貪婪，不知遠計，進利虜獲，退惜禾苗，謂我孤軍遠入，不能持久，不過進據臨朐，退守廣固，必不能守險清野，敢為諸君保之。」

translations.literal: The Xianbei are greedy and know no long view; advancing they prize booty, retreating they pity the grain in the fields. They will think our lone army has marched far and cannot last—at most they will advance to hold Linqu and fall back to defend Guanggu. They surely cannot hold the passes and clear the land. I dare guarantee this to you all."
translations.idiomatic: The Xianbei are greedy and shortsighted; advancing they prize booty, retreating they pity the grain. They will think our lone army cannot endure a long campaign—at most they will advance to Linqu and fall back to Guanggu. They will never hold the passes and clear the countryside. I stake my word on it."

sentences.zh: 南燕主超聞有晉師，引群臣會議。

translations.literal: The Southern Yan ruler Chao, hearing that Jin troops had come, summoned his ministers to council.
translations.idiomatic: When Murong Chao heard that Jin troops were coming, he summoned his ministers to council.

sentences.zh: 征虜將軍公孫五樓曰：「吳兵輕果，利在速戰，不可爭鋒。

translations.literal: General Who Conquers Barbarians Gongsun Wulou said: "Wu troops are light and swift, advantaged in quick battle—they must not be met head-on.
translations.idiomatic: General Who Conquers Barbarians Gongsun Wulou said, "Wu troops are light and swift and fight best in a quick battle—we must not meet them head-on.

sentences.zh: 宜據大峴，使不得入，曠日延時，沮其銳氣，然後徐簡精騎二千，循海而南，絕其糧道，別敕段暉帥兗州之眾，緣山東下，腹背擊之，此上策也。

translations.literal: We should hold Da'xian and keep them from entering, prolong the days and blunt their edge, then slowly select two thousand elite horsemen to follow the coast south and cut their supply line, and separately order Duan Hui to lead the Yanzhou forces down along the mountains to strike them front and rear—this is the best plan.
translations.idiomatic: Hold Da'xian and keep them out, wear down their edge over time, then pick two thousand elite horsemen to follow the coast south and cut their supply line, while Duan Hui leads the Yanzhou forces down the mountains to strike them front and rear—that is the best plan.

sentences.zh: 各命守宰依險自固，校其資儲之外，餘悉焚蕩，芟除禾苗，使敵無所資，彼僑軍無食，求戰不得，旬月之間，可以坐制，此中策也。

translations.literal: Order each magistrate to hold fast by terrain, and beyond what stores are counted burn and destroy the rest, cut down the grain so the enemy has nothing to draw on; their expeditionary army will have no food, cannot force battle, and within ten days or a month can be mastered sitting still—this is the middle plan.
translations.idiomatic: Order every magistrate to fortify the passes, burn everything beyond counted stores, and cut the grain so the enemy has nothing to live on; their expeditionary army will starve, cannot force battle, and within a month can be mastered without fighting—that is the middle plan.

sentences.zh: 縱賊入峴，出城逆戰，此下策也。」

translations.literal: Let the enemy into the pass and go out to meet them in battle—this is the worst plan."
translations.idiomatic: Let the enemy into the pass and meet them outside the walls—that is the worst plan."

sentences.zh: 超曰：「今歲星居齊，以天道推之，不戰自克。

translations.literal: Chao said: "This year the Year Star stands in Qi; by Heaven's way, without fighting we prevail.
translations.idiomatic: Chao said, "This year the Year Star stands in Qi; by Heaven's signs we prevail without fighting.

sentences.zh: 客主勢殊，以人事言之，彼遠來疲弊，勢不能久。

translations.literal: Host and guest differ in strength; in human terms they have come far and are worn out and cannot last.
translations.idiomatic: Host and guest differ in strength; in human terms they have marched far, are exhausted, and cannot last.

sentences.zh: 吾據五州之地，擁富庶之民，鐵騎萬群，麥禾布野，奈何芟苗徙民，鮮自蹙弱乎！

translations.literal: I hold five provinces, a rich and populous people, ten thousand groups of iron cavalry, wheat and grain spread over the fields—why cut the grain and move the people, scarcely weakening ourselves!
translations.idiomatic: I hold five provinces, a rich people, ten thousand iron cavalry, and grain spread across the fields—why cut the crops and move the people and weaken ourselves!

sentences.zh: 不如縱使入峴，以精騎蹂之，何憂不克！」

translations.literal: Better to let them into the pass and trample them with elite cavalry—why worry we will not win!"
translations.idiomatic: Better to let them through the pass and crush them with elite cavalry—why should we fail!"

sentences.zh: 輔國將軍廣寧王賀賴盧苦諫不從，退謂五樓曰：「必若此，亡無日矣！」

translations.literal: Prince of Guangling Helailu, General Who Assists the State, remonstrated bitterly but was not obeyed; withdrawing he said to Wulou: "If it must be thus, destruction is not far off!"
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Guangling Helailu, General Who Assists the State, remonstrated bitterly in vain; withdrawing he told Wulou, "If it goes this way, we are doomed!"

sentences.zh: 太尉桂林王鎮曰：「陛下必以騎兵利平地者，宜出峴逆戰，戰而不勝，猶可退守，不宜縱敵為峴，自棄險固也。」

translations.literal: Grand Marshal Prince of Guilin Zhen said: "If Your Majesty is certain cavalry excel on open ground, you should go out through the pass to meet them; if battle fails you can still fall back to defend—you should not let the enemy into the pass and abandon your strong positions."
translations.idiomatic: Grand Marshal Prince of Guilin Murong Zhen said, "If Your Majesty trusts cavalry on open ground, go out through the pass and fight; if you lose, you can still fall back—you should not let the enemy into the pass and throw away your strong positions."

sentences.zh: 超不從。

translations.literal: Chao would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Chao would not listen.

sentences.zh: 鎮出，謂韓言卓曰：「主上既不能逆戰卻敵，又不肯徙民清野，延敵入腹，坐待攻圍，酷似劉璋矣。

translations.literal: Zhen went out and said to Han Yanzhuo: "Our lord can neither meet the enemy in battle and drive him back, nor move the people and clear the land—he prolongs the enemy into our belly and sits waiting to be besieged. He is very like Liu Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen left and said to Han Yanzhuo, "Our lord will neither fight the enemy at the pass nor clear the countryside—he invites the enemy into our heartland and waits to be besieged. He is Liu Zhang all over again.

sentences.zh: 今年國滅，吾必死之。

translations.literal: This year the state perishes—I shall surely die for it.
translations.idiomatic: This year the state falls—I shall die for it.

sentences.zh: 卿中華之士，復為文身矣。」

translations.literal: You, a man of the Central States, will again be tattooed barbarian."
translations.idiomatic: You, a man of the Central States, will be tattooed barbarians again."

sentences.zh: 超聞之，大怒，收鎮下獄。

translations.literal: Chao heard of it, was greatly enraged, and had Zhen arrested and imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: When Chao heard, he was furious and had Zhen thrown into prison.

sentences.zh: 乃攝莒、梁父戌，修城隍，簡士馬，以待之。

translations.literal: He then took over the garrisons of Ju and Liangfu, repaired walls and moats, selected troops and horses, and waited.
translations.idiomatic: He then reinforced the garrisons at Ju and Liangfu, repaired walls and moats, mustered troops and horses, and waited.

sentences.zh: 劉裕過大峴，燕兵不出。

translations.literal: Liu Yu passed through Da'xian; Yan troops did not come out.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu passed through Da'xian; the Yan troops did not appear.

sentences.zh: 裕舉手指天，喜形於色。

translations.literal: Yu raised his hand toward Heaven, joy plain on his face.
translations.idiomatic: Yu raised his hand toward Heaven, joy plain on his face.

sentences.zh: 左右曰：「公未見敵而先喜，何也？」

translations.literal: Those beside him said: "My lord rejoices before you have seen the enemy—why?"
translations.idiomatic: His attendants said, "You rejoice before you have even seen the enemy—why?"

sentences.zh: 裕曰：「兵已過險，士有必死之志；

translations.literal: Yu said: "The army has passed the danger; the men have the will to die;
translations.idiomatic: Yu said, "The army has passed the danger; the men are ready to die;

sentences.zh: 餘糧棲畝，人無匱乏之憂。

translations.literal: surplus grain stands in the fields; the people have no fear of want.
translations.idiomatic: grain still stands in the fields; no one fears want.

sentences.zh: 虜已入吾掌中矣。」

translations.literal: The barbarians are already in the palm of my hand."
translations.idiomatic: The enemy is already in the palm of my hand."

sentences.zh: 六月，己巳，裕至東莞。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on jisi, Yu reached Dongguan.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on jisi, Yu reached Dongguan.

sentences.zh: 超先遣公孫五樓、賀賴盧及左將軍段暉等，將步騎五萬屯臨朐，聞晉兵入峴，自將步騎四萬往就之，使五樓帥騎進據巨蔑水。

translations.literal: Chao had earlier sent Gongsun Wulou, Helailu, and Left General Duan Hui and others with fifty thousand infantry and cavalry to camp at Linqu; hearing that Jin troops had entered the pass, he personally led forty thousand infantry and cavalry to join them and ordered Wulou to advance with cavalry and seize the Jumei River.
translations.idiomatic: Chao had already sent Gongsun Wulou, Helailu, and Left General Duan Hui with fifty thousand foot and horse to camp at Linqu; when he heard Jin troops had entered the pass, he personally led forty thousand to join them and ordered Wulou forward with cavalry to hold the Jumei River.

sentences.zh: 前鋒孟龍符與戰，破之，五樓退走。

translations.literal: The vanguard Meng Longfu fought them, defeated them, and Wulou retreated.
translations.idiomatic: Vanguard Meng Longfu fought them, routed them, and Wulou fled.

sentences.zh: 裕以車四千乘為左右翼，方軌徐進，與燕兵戰於臨朐南，日向昃，勝負猶未決。

translations.literal: Yu took four thousand chariots as left and right wings and advanced in measured ranks; he fought Yan troops south of Linqu until the sun slanted westward, and victory was still undecided.
translations.idiomatic: Yu formed four thousand chariots into left and right wings and advanced in steady ranks; he fought the Yan south of Linqu until late afternoon, and the outcome was still in doubt.

sentences.zh: 參軍胡籓言於裕曰：「燕悉兵出戰，臨朐城中留守必寡，願以奇兵從間道取其城，此韓信所以破趙也。」

translations.literal: Army Aide Hu Fan said to Yu: "Yan have sent out all their troops; the garrison in Linqu city must be few. I wish to take the city with a surprise force by a hidden path—this is how Han Xin broke Zhao."
translations.idiomatic: Army aide Hu Fan said to Yu, "Yan have thrown everything into the field; Linqu must be lightly held. Let me take the city by a hidden path with a surprise force—this is how Han Xin broke Zhao."

sentences.zh: 裕遣籓及諮議參軍檀韶、建威將軍河內向彌潛師出燕兵之後，攻臨朐，聲言輕兵自海道至矣，向彌擐甲先登，遂克之。

translations.literal: Yu sent Fan, Consultant Army Aide Tan Shao, and General Who Establishes Might Xiang Mi of Henei with a hidden column behind the Yan army to attack Linqu, spreading word that light troops had come by sea; Xiang Mi donned armor and was first up the wall, and they took it.
translations.idiomatic: Yu sent Fan, consultant army aide Tan Shao, and Xiang Mi of Henei, General Who Establishes Might, with a hidden column behind the Yan army against Linqu, spreading word that light troops had come by sea; Xiang Mi armored himself and was first over the wall, and they took the city.

sentences.zh: 超大驚，單騎就段暉於城南。

translations.literal: Chao was greatly alarmed and rode alone to join Duan Hui south of the city.
translations.idiomatic: Chao was terrified and rode alone to Duan Hui south of the city.

sentences.zh: 裕因縱兵奮擊，燕眾大敗，斬段暉等大將十餘人，超遁還廣固，獲其玉璽、輦及豹尾。

translations.literal: Yu then unleashed his troops in fierce attack; the Yan masses were greatly defeated, and more than ten great generals including Duan Hui were beheaded; Chao fled back to Guanggu, and Yu seized his jade seal, imperial carriage, and leopard-tail banners.
translations.idiomatic: Yu then unleashed his troops in a fierce assault; the Yan army was routed, and more than ten senior generals including Duan Hui were killed; Chao fled to Guanggu, and Yu seized his jade seal, imperial carriage, and leopard-tail banners.

sentences.zh: 裕乘勝逐北至廣固，丙子，克其大城，超收眾入保小城。

translations.literal: Yu pursued the victory north to Guanggu; on bingzi he took the outer city, and Chao gathered his forces into the inner citadel.
translations.idiomatic: Yu pursued north to Guanggu; on bingzi he captured the outer city, and Chao withdrew into the inner citadel with his remaining troops.

sentences.zh: 裕築長圍守之，圍高三丈，穿塹三重；

translations.literal: Yu built a long encirclement to besiege it, the rampart three zhang high, with three lines of ditches dug;
translations.idiomatic: Yu built a long siege line with ramparts three zhang high and three rings of ditches;

sentences.zh: 撫納降附，采拔賢俊，華、夷大悅。

translations.literal: he comforted and accepted those who surrendered, selected worthy men, and Chinese and barbarians alike were greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: he welcomed defectors, recruited talented men, and both Chinese and non-Chinese were greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 於是因齊地糧儲，悉停江、淮漕運。

translations.literal: Thereupon relying on Qi territory's grain stores, he halted all transport from the Jiang and Huai entirely.
translations.idiomatic: He then relied on Qi's grain stores and halted all transport from the Jiang and Huai.

sentences.zh: 超遣尚書郎張綱乞師於秦，赦桂林王鎮，以為錄尚書、都督中外諸軍事，引見，謝之，且問計焉。

translations.literal: Chao sent Master of Writing Attendant Zhang Gang to beg troops from Qin, pardoned Prince of Guilin Zhen, made him Recorder of the Masters of Writing and Commander-in-Chief of all armies at home and abroad, received him in audience, apologized to him, and asked his counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Chao sent Master of Writing attendant Zhang Gang to Qin to beg for troops, pardoned Prince of Guilin Murong Zhen, appointed him recorder of the Masters of Writing and commander-in-chief of all armies, received him in audience, apologized, and asked his advice.

sentences.zh: 鎮曰：「百姓之心，繫於一人。

translations.literal: Zhen said: "The hearts of the common people hang on one man.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen said, "The people's hearts hang on one man.

sentences.zh: 今陛下親董六師，奔敗而還。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty personally directed the six armies and returned in flight and defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty personally led the six armies and returned in defeat.

sentences.zh: 群臣離心，士民喪氣。

translations.literal: The ministers' hearts are divided, soldiers and people have lost their spirit.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers are divided, and soldiers and civilians have lost heart.

sentences.zh: 聞秦人自有內患，恐不暇分兵救人。

translations.literal: I hear the Qin people have troubles of their own and likely cannot spare troops to save us.
translations.idiomatic: I hear Qin has troubles of its own and likely cannot spare troops to save us.

sentences.zh: 散卒還者尚有數萬，宜悉出金帛以餌之，更決一戰。

translations.literal: Scattered soldiers who have returned still number several tens of thousands—you should spend all gold and silk to reward them and fight one more decisive battle.
translations.idiomatic: Scattered soldiers who have returned still number in the tens of thousands—you should spend all your gold and silk to reward them and fight one more decisive battle.

sentences.zh: 若天命助我，必能破敵；

translations.literal: If Heaven's mandate aids us, we can surely break the enemy;
translations.idiomatic: If Heaven aids us, we can surely break the enemy;

sentences.zh: 如其不然，死亦為美，比於閉門待盡，不猶愈乎！」

translations.literal: if not, death is still honorable—how is it not better than shutting the gates and waiting to perish!"
translations.idiomatic: if not, death is still honorable—is that not better than shutting the gates and waiting to die!"

sentences.zh: 司徒樂浪王惠曰：「不然。

translations.literal: Minister over the Masses Prince of Lelang Hui said: "Not so.
translations.idiomatic: Minister over the Masses Prince of Lelang Murong Hui said, "Not so.

sentences.zh: 晉兵乘勝，氣勢百倍，我以敗軍之卒當之，不亦難乎！

translations.literal: Jin troops ride victory and their momentum is a hundredfold; we meet them with defeated soldiers—is it not hard!
translations.idiomatic: Jin troops ride victory with momentum a hundredfold; we would meet them with defeated soldiers—is that not hopeless!

sentences.zh: 秦雖與勃勃相持，不足為患；

translations.literal: Though Qin is locked with Bobo, that is no great worry;
translations.idiomatic: Though Qin is locked in struggle with Bobo, that is no great worry;

sentences.zh: 且與我分據中原，勢如脣齒，安得不來相救！

translations.literal: moreover we share the Central Plains between us, close as lips and teeth—how can they fail to come and save us!
translations.idiomatic: moreover we share the Central Plains between us, close as lips and teeth—how can they fail to rescue us!

sentences.zh: 但不遣大臣則不能得重兵，尚書令韓范為燕、秦所重，宜遣乞師。」

translations.literal: But unless they send a great minister they cannot send a heavy army; Master of Writing Han Fan is esteemed by Yan and Qin alike—you should send him to beg troops."
translations.idiomatic: But unless they send a great minister they will not send a heavy army; Master of Writing Han Fan is esteemed by both Yan and Qin—you should send him to beg for troops."

sentences.zh: 超從之。

translations.literal: Chao followed this advice.
translations.idiomatic: Chao agreed.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，加劉裕北青、冀二州刺史。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Liu Yu was additionally made Inspector of Qing and Ji provinces north of the river.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, Liu Yu was additionally appointed inspector of Qing and Ji provinces north of the river.

sentences.zh: 南燕尚書略陽垣尊及弟京兆太守苗逾城來降，裕以為行參軍。

translations.literal: Southern Yan Master of Writing Yuan Zun of Liaoyang and his younger brother Miao, Administrator of Jingzhao, crossed the wall to surrender; Yu made them acting army aides.
translations.idiomatic: Southern Yan master of writing Yuan Zun of Liaoyang and his younger brother Miao, administrator of Jingzhao, climbed the wall to surrender; Yu made them acting army aides.

sentences.zh: 尊、苗皆超所委任以為腹心者也。

translations.literal: Zun and Miao were both men Chao had entrusted as his inner circle.
translations.idiomatic: Zun and Miao were both men Chao had trusted as his inner circle.

sentences.zh: 或謂裕曰：「張綱有巧思，若得綱使為攻具，廣固必可拔也。」

translations.literal: Someone said to Yu: "Zhang Gang has ingenious mind—if you get Gang to make siege engines, Guanggu can surely be taken."
translations.idiomatic: Someone said to Yu, "Zhang Gang is ingenious—if you get him to build siege engines, Guanggu can surely be taken."

sentences.zh: 會綱自長安還，太山太守申宣執之，送於裕。

translations.literal: As it happened Gang returned from Chang'an; Mount Tai Administrator Shen Xuan seized him and sent him to Yu.
translations.idiomatic: As it happened Gang returned from Chang'an; Mount Tai administrator Shen Xuan seized him and sent him to Yu.

sentences.zh: 裕升綱於樓車，使周城呼曰：「劉勃勃大破秦軍，無兵相救。」

translations.literal: Yu raised Gang on a tower cart and had him call around the city: "Helian Bobo has greatly defeated the Qin army; no troops can come to save you."
translations.idiomatic: Yu raised Gang on a tower cart and had him call around the walls, "Helian Bobo has routed the Qin army; no troops can save you."

sentences.zh: 城中莫不失色。

translations.literal: Everyone in the city lost color.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone in the city turned pale.

sentences.zh: 江南每發兵及遣使者至廣固，裕輒潛遣兵夜迎之，明日，張旗鳴鼓而至，北方之民執兵負糧歸裕者，日以千數。

translations.literal: Whenever the south of the Yang sent troops or envoys to Guanggu, Yu secretly sent troops by night to meet them; the next day banners were raised and drums sounded as they arrived—northerners who came to Yu bearing arms and grain numbered thousands each day.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the south sent troops or envoys to Guanggu, Yu secretly sent men by night to meet them; the next day they arrived with banners raised and drums beating—northerners coming to Yu with arms and grain numbered thousands each day.

sentences.zh: 圍城益急，張華、封愷皆為裕所獲，超請割大峴以南地為籓臣，裕不許。

translations.literal: The siege grew tighter; Zhang Hua and Feng Kai were both captured by Yu; Chao asked to cede all land south of Da'xian and become a vassal—Yu would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: The siege tightened; Zhang Hua and Feng Kai were captured by Yu; Chao offered to cede all land south of Da'xian and become a vassal—Yu refused.

sentences.zh: 秦王興遣使謂裕曰：「慕容氏相與鄰好，今晉攻之急，秦已遣鐵騎十萬屯洛陽；

translations.literal: King Xing of Qin sent an envoy to say to Yu: "The Murong clan and we are friendly neighbors; now Jin presses hard in attack—Qin has already sent one hundred thousand iron cavalry to camp at Luoyang;
translations.idiomatic: King Xing of Qin sent an envoy to Yu, "The Murong clan and we are friendly neighbors; Jin presses hard in attack—Qin has already sent one hundred thousand iron cavalry to camp at Luoyang;

sentences.zh: 晉軍不還，當長驅而進。」

translations.literal: if Jin troops do not withdraw, we shall drive forward at full speed."
translations.idiomatic: if Jin troops do not withdraw, we shall drive forward at full speed."

sentences.zh: 裕呼秦使者謂曰：「語汝姚興：我克燕之後，息兵三年，當取關、洛。

translations.literal: Yu called the Qin envoy and said: "Tell your Yao Xing: after I take Yan I shall rest the armies three years, then take Guan and Luo.
translations.idiomatic: Yu called the Qin envoy and said, "Tell your Yao Xing: after I take Yan I shall rest the armies three years, then take Guanzhong and Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 今能自送，便可速來！」

translations.literal: If you can deliver yourselves now, come quickly!"
translations.idiomatic: If you want to deliver yourselves now, come quickly!"

sentences.zh: 劉穆之聞有秦使，馳入見裕，而秦使者已去。

translations.literal: Liu Muzhi, hearing there was a Qin envoy, galloped in to see Yu, but the Qin envoy had already left.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Muzhi, hearing there was a Qin envoy, galloped in to see Yu, but the envoy had already left.

sentences.zh: 裕以所言告穆之，穆之尤之曰：「常日事無大小，必賜預謀，此宜善詳，去何遽爾答之！

translations.literal: Yu told Muzhi what he had said; Muzhi blamed him: "On ordinary days nothing great or small fails to win your consultation—this should have been weighed carefully; why answer so hastily as he left!
translations.idiomatic: Yu told Muzhi what he had said; Muzhi reproached him, "On ordinary days you consult me on everything great and small—this deserved careful thought; why answer so hastily as he left!

sentences.zh: 此語不足以威敵，適足以怒之。

translations.literal: These words are not enough to awe the enemy—they only suffice to anger him.
translations.idiomatic: Those words will not awe the enemy—they will only anger him.

sentences.zh: 若廣固未下，羌寇奄至，不審何以待之？」

translations.literal: If Guanggu is not yet taken and Qiang raiders arrive suddenly, I do not know how you will deal with it?"
translations.idiomatic: If Guanggu is not yet taken and Qiang raiders arrive suddenly, how will you deal with it?"

sentences.zh: 裕笑曰：「此是兵機，非卿所解，故不相語耳。

translations.literal: Yu smiled and said: "This is military timing—not something you understand, which is why I did not tell you.
translations.idiomatic: Yu smiled and said, "This is military timing—not something you understand, which is why I did not tell you.

sentences.zh: 夫兵貴神速，彼若審能赴救，必畏我知，寧容先遣信命，逆設此言！

translations.literal: In war speed is precious; if they could truly come to the rescue, they would fear we knew—how would they allow sending envoys first and setting up this talk in advance!
translations.idiomatic: In war speed is precious; if they could truly rescue Yan, they would fear we knew—why send envoys first with this bluff!

sentences.zh: 是自張大之辭也。

translations.literal: This is language that puffs themselves up.
translations.idiomatic: This is empty bluster.

sentences.zh: 晉師不出，為日久矣。

translations.literal: Jin armies have not marched out for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: Jin armies have not marched out for a long time.

sentences.zh: 羌見伐齊，始將內懼。

translations.literal: The Qiang, seeing Qi attacked, will begin to fear within.
translations.idiomatic: The Qiang, seeing us attack Qi, will begin to fear for themselves.

sentences.zh: 自保不暇，何能救人邪！」

translations.literal: They cannot spare effort even to save themselves—how can they save others!"
translations.idiomatic: They cannot even save themselves—how can they save others!"

sentences.zh: 乞伏乾歸復即秦王位，大赦，改元更始，公卿以下皆復本位。

translations.literal: Qifu Qian'gui again assumed the title King of Qin, proclaimed a general amnesty, changed the era name to Gengshi, and all from dukes and ministers down resumed their original posts.
translations.idiomatic: Qifu Qian'gui again assumed the title King of Qin, proclaimed a general amnesty, changed the era name to Gengshi, and all officials from dukes and ministers down resumed their original posts.

sentences.zh: 慕容氏在魏者百餘家，謀逃去，魏主珪盡殺之。

translations.literal: More than a hundred Murong households in Wei plotted to flee; the Wei ruler Gui had them all killed.
translations.idiomatic: More than a hundred Murong households in Wei plotted to flee; Emperor Gui of Wei had them all killed.

sentences.zh: 初，魏太尉穆崇與衛王儀伏甲謀弒魏主珪，不果；

translations.literal: Earlier, Wei Grand Marshal Mu Chong and Prince of Wei Yi had hidden armed men to assassinate the Wei ruler Gui, but it did not succeed;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Wei grand marshal Mu Chong and Prince of Wei Murong Yi had plotted to assassinate Emperor Gui with hidden armed men, but failed;

sentences.zh: 珪惜崇、儀之功，秘而不問。

translations.literal: Gui valued Chong and Yi's merit and kept it secret without inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: Gui valued their merit and kept the matter secret.

sentences.zh: 及珪有疾，多殺大臣，儀自疑而出亡，追獲之。

translations.literal: When Gui fell ill and killed many ministers, Yi suspected himself and fled; he was pursued and captured.
translations.idiomatic: When Gui fell ill and killed many ministers, Yi grew suspicious and fled; he was pursued and captured.

sentences.zh: 八月，賜儀死。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Yi was ordered to die.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, Yi was ordered to take his own life.

sentences.zh: 封融詣劉裕降。

translations.literal: Feng Rong went to Liu Yu and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Rong went to Liu Yu and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 九月，加劉裕太尉，裕固辭。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Liu Yu was additionally made Grand Marshal; Yu firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, Liu Yu was offered the post of grand marshal; Yu firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 秦王興自將擊夏王勃勃，至貳城，遣安遠將軍姚詳等分督租運。

translations.literal: King Xing of Qin personally led an attack on the Xia king Bobo, reached Ercheng, and sent General Who Pacifies the Distance Yao Xiang and others to oversee grain transport in separate divisions.
translations.idiomatic: King Xing of Qin personally led an attack on Xia king Helian Bobo, reached Ercheng, and sent Yao Xiang, General Who Pacifies the Distance, and others to oversee grain transport in separate divisions.

sentences.zh: 勃勃乘虛奄至，興懼，欲輕騎就詳等。

translations.literal: Bobo seized the moment of weakness and came suddenly; Xing was afraid and wished to go with light cavalry to join Xiang and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Bobo seized the moment and struck suddenly; Xing was afraid and wished to ride with light cavalry to join Xiang.

sentences.zh: 右僕射韋華曰：「若鑾輿一動，眾心駭懼，必不戰自潰，詳營亦未必可至也。」

translations.literal: Right Vice Director Wei Hua said: "If the imperial carriage moves, the army's hearts will be terrified and they will collapse without fighting; Xiang's camp may not be reachable either."
translations.idiomatic: Right Vice Director Wei Hua said, "If the imperial carriage moves, the army will panic and collapse without fighting, and Xiang's camp may not be reachable either."

sentences.zh: 興與勃勃戰，秦兵大敗，將軍姚榆生為勃勃所擒，左將軍姚文宗等力戰，勃勃乃退，興還長安。

translations.literal: Xing fought Bobo; Qin troops were greatly defeated; General Yao Yusheng was captured by Bobo; Left General Yao Wenzong and others fought fiercely, and Bobo then withdrew; Xing returned to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Xing fought Bobo; the Qin army was routed; General Yao Yusheng was captured; Left General Yao Wenzong and others fought fiercely until Bobo withdrew; Xing returned to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 勃勃復攻秦敕奇堡、黃石固、我羅城，皆拔之，徙七千餘家於大城，以其丞相右地代領幽州牧以鎮之。

translations.literal: Bobo again attacked the Qin forts Chiqibao, Huangshigu, and Woluocheng, took them all, moved more than seven thousand households to Dacheng, and had his chancellor Youdidai serve as Governor of You province to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: Bobo again attacked the Qin forts Chiqibao, Huangshigu, and Woluocheng, took them all, moved more than seven thousand households to Dacheng, and had his chancellor Youdidai serve as governor of You province to garrison the region.

sentences.zh: 初，興遣衛將軍姚強帥步騎一萬，隨韓范往就姚紹於洛陽，並兵以救南燕，及為勃勃所敗，追強兵還長安。

translations.literal: Earlier, Xing had sent General of the Guards Yao Qiang at the head of ten thousand infantry and cavalry to follow Han Fan to join Yao Shao at Luoyang and combine forces to save Southern Yan; when he was defeated by Bobo, Qiang's troops were recalled to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Xing had sent Yao Qiang, General of the Guards, with ten thousand foot and horse to follow Han Fan and join Yao Shao at Luoyang to rescue Southern Yan; when Xing was defeated by Bobo, Qiang's troops were recalled to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 韓范歎曰：「天滅燕矣！」

translations.literal: Han Fan sighed and said: "Heaven is destroying Yan!"
translations.idiomatic: Han Fan sighed, "Heaven is destroying Yan!"

sentences.zh: 南燕尚書張俊自長安還，降於劉裕，因說裕曰：「燕人所恃者，謂韓范必能致秦師也，今得范以示之，燕必降矣。」

translations.literal: Southern Yan Master of Writing Zhang Jun returned from Chang'an and surrendered to Liu Yu; he therefore said to Yu: "What the Yan people rely on is the belief that Han Fan can bring Qin troops; now if you get Fan and show him, Yan will surely surrender."
translations.idiomatic: Southern Yan master of writing Zhang Jun returned from Chang'an and surrendered to Liu Yu, telling him, "The Yan rely on the belief that Han Fan can bring Qin troops; show them Fan in captivity and Yan will surrender."

sentences.zh: 裕乃表範為散騎常侍，且以書招之，長水校尉王蒲勸范奔秦，范曰：「劉裕起布衣，滅桓玄，復晉室；

translations.literal: Yu then memorialized making Fan Attendant Cavalier at Large and also sent a letter to win him; Colonel of the Changshui Wang Pu urged Fan to flee to Qin; Fan said: "Liu Yu rose from common cloth, destroyed Huan Xuan, and restored the Jin house;
translations.idiomatic: Yu memorialized Fan as attendant cavalier at large and sent a letter to win him; Colonel of the Changshui Wang Pu urged Fan to flee to Qin; Fan said, "Liu Yu rose from common birth, destroyed Huan Xuan, and restored the Jin house;

sentences.zh: 今興師伐燕，所向崩潰，此殆天授，非人力也。

translations.literal: now he raises armies against Yan and wherever he goes there is collapse—this is likely Heaven's gift, not human power.
translations.idiomatic: now he campaigns against Yan and wherever he goes armies collapse—this is Heaven's gift, not human power.

sentences.zh: 燕亡，則秦為之次矣，吾不可以再辱。」

translations.literal: When Yan perishes, Qin will be next—I cannot suffer disgrace a second time."
translations.idiomatic: When Yan falls, Qin will be next—I cannot suffer disgrace twice."

sentences.zh: 遂降於裕。

translations.literal: He then surrendered to Yu.
translations.idiomatic: He then surrendered to Yu.

sentences.zh: 裕將范循城，城中人情離沮。

translations.literal: Yu led Fan around the city walls; morale in the city split and sank.
translations.idiomatic: Yu paraded Fan around the walls; morale in the city collapsed.

sentences.zh: 或勸燕主超誅范家，超以范弟言卓盡忠無貳，並范家赦之。

translations.literal: Someone urged the Yan ruler Chao to execute Fan's family; Chao, because Fan's younger brother Yanzhuo was utterly loyal without duplicity, pardoned the whole Fan family.
translations.idiomatic: Someone urged Murong Chao to execute Fan's family; Chao, because Fan's younger brother Yanzhuo had been utterly loyal, pardoned the whole Fan family.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，段宏自魏奔於裕。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, Duan Hong fled from Wei to Yu.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, Duan Hong fled from Wei to Liu Yu.

sentences.zh: 張綱為裕造攻具，盡諸奇巧。

translations.literal: Zhang Gang made siege engines for Yu with every sort of ingenious device.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Gang built siege engines for Yu with every sort of ingenious device.

sentences.zh: 超怒，縣綱母於城上，支解之。

translations.literal: Chao was enraged, hung Gang's mother on the wall, and dismembered her.
translations.idiomatic: Chao was enraged, hung Gang's mother on the wall, and dismembered her.

sentences.zh: 西秦王乾歸立夫人邊氏為王后，世子熾磐為太子，仍命熾磐都督中外諸軍、錄尚書事。

translations.literal: The Western Qin king Qian'gui installed Lady Bian as queen, the heir Chipan as crown prince, and still ordered Chipan to command all armies at home and abroad and record Masters of Writing affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Western Qin king Qian'gui installed Lady Bian as queen and his heir Chipan as crown prince, and ordered Chipan to command all armies and record Masters of Writing affairs.

sentences.zh: 以屋引破光為河州刺史，鎮枹罕；

translations.literal: He made Wuyin Poguang Governor of He province to garrison Fuhan;
translations.idiomatic: He made Wuyin Poguang governor of He province to garrison Fuhan;

sentences.zh: 以南安焦遺為太子太師，與參軍國大謀。

translations.literal: he made Jiao Yi of Nan'an Grand Tutor to the Heir and had him join the army aide in planning state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: he made Jiao Yi of Nan'an grand tutor to the heir and had him join the army aide in state planning.

sentences.zh: 乾歸曰：「焦生非特名儒，乃王佐之才也。」

translations.literal: Qian'gui said: "Master Jiao is not only a famous Confucian—he has talent to assist a king."
translations.idiomatic: Qian'gui said, "Master Jiao is not only a famous Confucian—he has the talent to assist a king."

sentences.zh: 謂熾磐曰：「汝事之當如事吾。」

translations.literal: He told Chipan: "In serving him you should be as in serving me."
translations.idiomatic: He told Chipan, "Serve him as you serve me."

sentences.zh: 熾磐拜遺於床下。

translations.literal: Chipan bowed to Yi below the couch.
translations.idiomatic: Chipan bowed to Yi below the couch.

sentences.zh: 遺子華至孝，乾歸欲以女妻之，辭曰：「凡娶妻者，欲與之共事二親也。

translations.literal: Yi's son Hua was utmost in filial piety; Qian'gui wished to give him his daughter in marriage; Hua declined, saying: "In general one takes a wife wishing to share in serving both parents.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's son Hua was deeply filial; Qian'gui wished to give him his daughter in marriage; Hua declined, saying, "One takes a wife to share in serving both parents.

sentences.zh: 今以王姬之貴，下嫁蓬茅之士，誠非其匹，臣懼其闕於中饋，非所願也。」

translations.literal: Now with a royal princess's nobility to marry down to a thatched-hut scholar, it is truly no match; your servant fears she would fail in household duties—it is not what I wish."
translations.idiomatic: Now a royal princess marrying down to a humble scholar is truly no match; I fear she would fail in household duties—it is not what I wish."

sentences.zh: 乾歸曰：「卿之所行，古人之事，孤女不足以強卿。」

translations.literal: Qian'gui said: "What you do is the conduct of ancients; my daughter is not enough to force you."
translations.idiomatic: Qian'gui said, "What you do is the conduct of the ancients; my daughter is not enough to force you."

sentences.zh: 乃以為尚書民部郎。

translations.literal: He then made him Master of Writing, People's Section.
translations.idiomatic: He then made him master of writing for the people's section.

sentences.zh: 北燕王雲自以無功德而居大位，內懷危懼，常畜養壯士以為腹心爪牙。

translations.literal: The Northern Yan king Yun, believing himself without merit yet holding the great position, harbored fear within and constantly kept strong men as his inner heart and claws.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Yan king Murong Yun, believing himself without merit yet holding the throne, lived in inward fear and constantly kept strong men as his inner guard.

sentences.zh: 寵臣離班、桃仁專典禁衛，賞賜以巨萬計，衣食起居皆與之同，而班、仁志願無厭，猶有怨憾。

translations.literal: Favored ministers Li Ban and Tao Ren alone controlled the palace guard; rewards ran to tens of thousands, food, clothing, and daily life were all shared with them—yet Ban and Ren's desires knew no satiety and they still harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Favored ministers Li Ban and Tao Ren alone controlled the palace guard; rewards ran to tens of thousands, and they shared Yun's food, clothing, and daily life—yet Ban and Ren were never satisfied and still harbored resentment.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，雲臨東堂，班、仁懷劍執紙而入，稱有所啟。

translations.literal: On wuchen, Yun came to the Eastern Hall; Ban and Ren entered bearing swords and holding paper, saying they had something to report.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen, Yun came to the Eastern Hall; Ban and Ren entered with swords and paper, saying they had something to report.

sentences.zh: 班抽劍擊雲，雲以幾扞之，仁從旁擊雲，弒之。

translations.literal: Ban drew his sword and struck Yun; Yun used a table to ward it off; Ren struck Yun from the side and assassinated him.
translations.idiomatic: Ban drew his sword and struck Yun; Yun warded him off with a table; Ren struck Yun from the side and assassinated him.

sentences.zh: 馮跋升洪光門以觀變，帳下督張泰、李桑言於跋曰：「此豎勢何所至，請為公斬之！」

translations.literal: Feng Ba ascended the Hongguang Gate to observe the disturbance; Supervisors of the Tent Zhang Tai and Li Sang said to Ba: "Where can these villains' momentum go—allow us to behead them for you!"
translations.idiomatic: Feng Ba ascended the Hongguang Gate to observe the disturbance; tent supervisors Zhang Tai and Li Sang said to Ba, "Where can these villains go—let us behead them for you!"

sentences.zh: 乃奮劍而下，桑斬班於西門，泰殺仁於庭中。

translations.literal: They then seized swords and came down; Sang beheaded Ban at the western gate, Tai killed Ren in the courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: They seized their swords and came down; Sang beheaded Ban at the western gate, Tai killed Ren in the courtyard.

sentences.zh: 眾推跋為主，跋以讓其弟范陽公素弗，素弗不可。

translations.literal: The masses urged Ba as lord; Ba yielded to his younger brother the Duke of Fanyang Sufu, and Sufu would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: The crowd urged Ba as ruler; Ba yielded to his younger brother Sufu, Duke of Fanyang, and Sufu refused.

sentences.zh: 跋乃即天王位於昌黎，大赦，詔曰：「陳氏代姜，不改齊國。

translations.literal: Ba then assumed the Heavenly King throne at Changli, proclaimed a general amnesty, and issued an edict: "When the Chen clan replaced the Jiang, they did not change the state of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Ba then assumed the Heavenly King throne at Changli, proclaimed a general amnesty, and issued an edict, "When the Chen clan replaced the Jiang, they did not change the state of Qi.

sentences.zh: 宜即國號曰燕。」

translations.literal: We should take the state name Yan."
translations.idiomatic: We should take the state name Yan."

sentences.zh: 改元太平，謚雲曰惠懿皇帝。

translations.literal: He changed the era name to Taiping and gave Yun the posthumous title Emperor Huiyi.
translations.idiomatic: He changed the era name to Taiping and gave Yun the posthumous title Emperor Huiyi.

sentences.zh: 跋尊母張氏為太后，立妻孫氏為王后，子永為太子，以范陽公素弗為車騎大將軍、錄尚書事，孫護為尚書令，張興為左僕射，汲郡公弘為右僕射，廣川公萬泥為幽、平二州牧，上谷公乳陳為並、青二州牧。

translations.literal: Ba honored his mother Lady Zhang as Empress Dowager, installed his wife Lady Sun as queen, his son Yong as crown prince, made Duke of Fanyang Sufu General of Chariots and Cavalry and Recorder of the Masters of Writing, Sun Hu Master of Writing, Zhang Xing Left Vice Director, Duke of Ji commandery Hong Right Vice Director, Duke of Guangchuan Wanni Governor of You and Ping provinces, Duke of Shanggu Ruchen Governor of Bing and Qing provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Ba honored his mother Lady Zhang as empress dowager, installed his wife Lady Sun as queen and his son Yong as crown prince, made Sufu, Duke of Fanyang, general of chariots and cavalry and recorder of the Masters of Writing, Sun Hu master of writing, Zhang Xing left vice director, Hong, Duke of Ji, right vice director, Wanni, Duke of Guangchuan, governor of You and Ping provinces, and Ruchen, Duke of Shanggu, governor of Bing and Qing provinces.

sentences.zh: 素弗少豪俠放蕩，嘗請婚於尚書左丞韓業，業拒之。

translations.literal: Sufu in youth was bold, chivalrous, and unrestrained; he once asked marriage of Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Han Ye, and Ye refused him.
translations.idiomatic: Sufu in youth was bold and unrestrained; he once asked to marry the daughter of Han Ye, left vice director of the Masters of Writing, and Ye refused.

sentences.zh: 及為宰輔，待業尤厚。

translations.literal: When he became chief minister, he treated Ye with especial generosity.
translations.idiomatic: When he became chief minister, he treated Ye with especial generosity.

sentences.zh: 好申拔舊門，謙恭儉約，以身帥下，百僚憚之，論者美其有宰相之度。

translations.literal: He liked to promote old families, was humble, respectful, and frugal, led subordinates by his own example, the hundred officials feared him, and commentators praised him as having a chancellor's measure.
translations.idiomatic: He liked to promote old families, was humble and frugal, led subordinates by example, the officials feared him, and commentators praised him as having a chancellor's measure.

sentences.zh: 魏主珪將立齊王嗣為太子。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler Gui was about to install Prince of Qi Si as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gui of Wei was about to install Prince of Qi Murong Si as crown prince.

sentences.zh: 魏故事，凡立嗣子，輒先殺其母，乃賜嗣母劉貴人死。

translations.literal: By Wei precedent, whenever an heir was installed, his mother was first killed; therefore Si's mother Lady Liu the Honored was ordered to die.
translations.idiomatic: By Wei precedent, whenever an heir was installed, his mother was first killed; therefore Si's mother, Lady Liu, was ordered to die.

sentences.zh: 珪召嗣諭之曰：「漢武帝殺鉤弋夫人，以防母后預政，外家為亂也。

translations.literal: Gui summoned Si and instructed him: "Emperor Wu of Han killed Lady Gouyi to prevent the empress dowager from interfering in government and the maternal kin from causing disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Gui summoned Si and told him, "Emperor Wu of Han killed Lady Gouyi to prevent the empress dowager from interfering in government and the maternal kin from causing disorder.

sentences.zh: 汝當繼統，吾故遠跡古人，為國家長久之計耳。」

translations.literal: You are to succeed to the succession; I therefore follow the ancients from afar, for the state's long-lasting plan."
translations.idiomatic: You are to succeed to the throne; I follow the ancients for the state's long-term good."

sentences.zh: 嗣性孝，哀泣不自勝。

translations.literal: Si was filial by nature and wept in grief beyond control.
translations.idiomatic: Si was filial by nature and wept uncontrollably.

sentences.zh: 珪怒之。

translations.literal: Gui was angry with him.
translations.idiomatic: Gui was angry with him.

sentences.zh: 嗣還捨，日夜號泣，珪知而復召之。

translations.literal: Si returned to his quarters and wept day and night; Gui learned of it and summoned him again.
translations.idiomatic: Si returned to his quarters and wept day and night; Gui learned of it and summoned him again.

sentences.zh: 左右曰：「上怒甚，入將不測，不如且避之，俟上怒解而入。」

translations.literal: Those beside him said: "The sovereign is very angry; if you enter the outcome is unpredictable—better for now to avoid him and wait until his anger eases before entering."
translations.idiomatic: His attendants said, "The sovereign is very angry; if you go in the outcome is unpredictable—better avoid him until his anger eases."

sentences.zh: 嗣乃逃匿於外，帷帳下代人車路頭、京兆王洛兒二人隨之。

translations.literal: Si then fled and hid outside; two men of his tent guard, Chelutou of Dairen and Wang Luo'er of Jingzhao, followed him.
translations.idiomatic: Si then fled and hid outside; two of his tent guards, Chelutou of Dairen and Wang Luo'er of Jingzhao, went with him.

sentences.zh: 初，珪如賀蘭部，見獻明賀太后之妹美，言於賀太后，請納之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Gui went to the Helan tribe, he saw that the younger sister of Empress Dowager He Xianming was beautiful; he spoke to Empress Dowager He and asked to take her in.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Gui visited the Helan tribe, he saw that Empress Dowager He Xianming's younger sister was beautiful; he spoke to the empress dowager and asked to take her as consort.

sentences.zh: 賀太后曰：「不可。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager He said: "It cannot be.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager He said, "No.

sentences.zh: 是過美，必有不善。

translations.literal: She is excessively beautiful; there must be something ill-omened.
translations.idiomatic: She is too beautiful; something ill must come of it.

sentences.zh: 且已有夫，不可奪也。」

translations.literal: Moreover she already has a husband; she must not be taken away."
translations.idiomatic: Besides, she already has a husband—you must not take her from him."

sentences.zh: 珪密令人殺其夫而納之，生清河王紹。

translations.literal: Gui secretly had someone kill her husband and took her in; she bore Prince of Qinghe Shao.
translations.idiomatic: Gui secretly had her husband killed and took her in; she bore Prince of Qinghe Shao.

sentences.zh: 紹凶很無賴，好輕游里巷，劫剝行人以為樂。

translations.literal: Shao was fierce, cruel, and worthless; he liked to roam lightly through lanes and alleys, robbing and stripping passersby for sport.
translations.idiomatic: Shao was savage and worthless; he liked to roam the streets, robbing passersby for amusement.

sentences.zh: 珪怒之，嘗倒懸井中，垂死，乃出之。

translations.literal: Gui was angry with him; once he hung him upside down in a well until near death, then pulled him out.
translations.idiomatic: Gui was furious with him; once he hung him head-down in a well until he was nearly dead, then pulled him out.

sentences.zh: 齊王嗣屢誨責之，紹由是與嗣不協。

translations.literal: Prince of Qi Si repeatedly admonished and rebuked him; Shao therefore fell out with Si.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Qi Si repeatedly admonished and rebuked him; from this Shao and Si were at odds.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，珪譴責賀夫人，囚，將殺之。

translations.literal: On wuchen, Gui reproached Lady He, imprisoned her, and was about to kill her.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen, Gui rebuked Lady He, had her imprisoned, and was about to execute her.

sentences.zh: 會日暮，未決。

translations.literal: Evening came and no decision had been made.
translations.idiomatic: Evening came, and no decision had been reached.

sentences.zh: 夫人密使告紹曰：「汝何以救我？」

translations.literal: The lady secretly sent word to Shao, saying: "How will you save me?"
translations.idiomatic: The lady secretly sent word to Shao: "How will you save me?"

sentences.zh: 左右以珪殘忍，人人危懼。

translations.literal: Those around them, knowing Gui's cruelty, all feared for their lives.
translations.idiomatic: Those around them, knowing Gui's cruelty, all lived in dread.

sentences.zh: 紹年十六，夜，與帳下及宦者宮人數人通謀，逾垣入宮，至天安殿。

translations.literal: Shao was sixteen; at night he secretly conspired with several tent guards, eunuchs, and palace women, scaled the wall and entered the palace, and reached the Tian'an Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Shao was sixteen; that night he secretly conspired with several tent guards, eunuchs, and palace women, scaled the palace wall, and reached the Tian'an Hall.

sentences.zh: 左右呼曰：「賊至！」

translations.literal: Those beside him cried: "Bandits have come!"
translations.idiomatic: Those beside him cried, "Bandits!"

sentences.zh: 珪驚起，求弓刀不獲，遂弒之。

translations.literal: Gui started up in alarm, sought bow and blade but could not find them, and was assassinated.
translations.idiomatic: Gui started up in alarm, searched for bow and blade but found none, and was assassinated.

sentences.zh: 己巳，宮門至日中不開。

translations.literal: On jisi, the palace gates remained unopened until noon.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi, the palace gates stayed shut until noon.

sentences.zh: 紹稱詔，集百官於端門前，北面立。

translations.literal: Shao, claiming an imperial edict, gathered the hundred officials before the Duan Gate and had them stand facing north.
translations.idiomatic: Shao, claiming an imperial edict, gathered the officials before the Duan Gate and had them stand facing north.

sentences.zh: 紹從門扉間謂百官曰：「我有叔父，亦有兄，公卿欲從誰？」

translations.literal: From between the gate leaves Shao said to the hundred officials: "I have an uncle and I also have an elder brother—which of them do you, lords and ministers, wish to follow?"
translations.idiomatic: From between the gate leaves Shao said to the officials, "I have an uncle and I have an elder brother—which do you lords and ministers mean to follow?"

sentences.zh: 眾愕然失色，莫有對者。

translations.literal: The crowd was stunned and turned pale; no one answered.
translations.idiomatic: All were stunned and turned pale; no one replied.

sentences.zh: 良久，南平公長孫嵩曰：「從王。」

translations.literal: After a long silence, Changsun Song, Duke of Nanping, said: "We follow the prince."
translations.idiomatic: After a long silence, Changsun Song, Duke of Nanping, said, "We follow the prince."

sentences.zh: 眾乃知宮車晏駕，而不測其故，莫敢出聲，唯陰平公烈大哭而去。

translations.literal: The crowd then knew the imperial carriage had halted, but could not fathom the reason; none dared speak; only Lie, Duke of Yinping, wept loudly and left.
translations.idiomatic: The crowd then knew the emperor was dead, but could not guess why; none dared speak—only Lie, Duke of Yinping, wept aloud and left.

sentences.zh: 烈，儀之弟也。

translations.literal: Lie was the younger brother of Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Lie was Yi's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 於是朝野恟恟，人懷異志。

translations.literal: Then court and countryside were in uproar, and men harbored divergent intents.
translations.idiomatic: Then court and countryside were in uproar, and men nursed private designs.

sentences.zh: 肥如侯賀護舉烽於安陽城北，賀蘭部人皆赴之，其餘諸部亦各屯聚。

translations.literal: He Hu, Marquis of Feiru, raised beacon fires north of Anyang city; the Helan tribesmen all rushed to him, and the remaining tribes likewise gathered and encamped separately.
translations.idiomatic: He Hu, Marquis of Feiru, raised beacon fires north of Anyang; Helan tribesmen all rallied to him, and the other tribes likewise gathered and encamped.

sentences.zh: 紹聞人情不安，大出布帛賜王已下，崔宏獨不受。

translations.literal: When Shao heard that popular sentiment was unsettled, he distributed cloth and silk lavishly, bestowing it on princes and below; Cui Hong alone refused to accept.
translations.idiomatic: When Shao heard the people were unsettled, he distributed cloth and silk lavishly to princes and all below; Cui Hong alone refused.

sentences.zh: 齊王嗣聞變，乃自外還，晝伏匿山中，夜宿王洛兒家。

translations.literal: Prince of Qi Si, hearing of the disturbance, returned from outside; by day he hid in the mountains, by night he lodged at Wang Luo'er's home.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Qi Si, hearing of the coup, came back from outside; by day he hid in the mountains, by night he stayed at Wang Luo'er's house.

sentences.zh: 洛兒鄰人李道潛奉給嗣，民間頗知之，喜而相告；

translations.literal: Luo'er's neighbor Li Daosqian secretly supplied Si; this became rather widely known among the people, who rejoiced and told one another;
translations.idiomatic: Luo'er's neighbor Li Daosqian secretly supplied Si; word spread among the people, who rejoiced and told one another;

sentences.zh: 紹聞之，收道，斬之。

translations.literal: Shao heard of it, seized Dao, and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Shao heard of it, seized Dao, and executed him.

sentences.zh: 紹募人求訪嗣，欲殺之。

translations.literal: Shao recruited men to search for Si, intending to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Shao recruited men to hunt for Si, intending to kill him.

sentences.zh: 獵郎叔孫俊與宗室疏屬拓跋磨渾自雲知嗣所在，紹使帳下二人與之偕往；

translations.literal: Hunting officer Shusun Jun and a distant kinsman of the imperial clan, Tuoba Mo Hun, themselves claimed to know where Si was; Shao sent two of his tent guards to go with them;
translations.idiomatic: Hunting officer Shusun Jun and a distant imperial kinsman, Tuoba Mo Hun, claimed to know where Si was; Shao sent two tent guards to go with them;

sentences.zh: 俊、靡渾得出，即執帳下詣嗣，斬之。

translations.literal: Jun and Mo Hun were able to get out, immediately seized the tent guards, brought them to Si, and beheaded them.
translations.idiomatic: Jun and Mo Hun got away, seized the tent guards, brought them to Si, and had them executed.

sentences.zh: 俊，建之子也。

translations.literal: Jun was the son of Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Jun was Jian's son.

sentences.zh: 王洛兒為嗣往來平城，通問大臣，夜，告安遠將軍安同等。

translations.literal: Wang Luo'er went back and forth to Pingcheng for Si, communicating with the great ministers; at night he informed An Tong, general who pacifies the distant.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Luo'er traveled back and forth to Pingcheng for Si, contacting the great ministers; at night he informed General Who Pacifies the Distant An Tong.

sentences.zh: 眾聞之，翕然響應，爭出奉迎。

translations.literal: When the masses heard, they responded as one and rushed out to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: When word spread, men responded as one and rushed out to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 嗣至城西，衛士執紹送之。

translations.literal: When Si reached the west of the city, the guard soldiers seized Shao and delivered him.
translations.idiomatic: When Si reached the west of the city, the guards seized Shao and brought him in.

sentences.zh: 嗣殺紹及其母賀氏，並誅紹帳下及宦官宮人為內應者十餘人。

translations.literal: Si killed Shao and his mother Lady He, and together executed more than ten of Shao's tent guards and eunuch palace women who had acted as inside accomplices.
translations.idiomatic: Si killed Shao and his mother Lady He, and executed more than ten of Shao's tent guards and eunuch palace women who had served as inside accomplices.

sentences.zh: 其先犯乘輿者，群臣臠食之。

translations.literal: Those who had first violated the imperial carriage—the ministers cut flesh from their bodies and ate it.
translations.idiomatic: Those who had first laid hands on the imperial carriage—the ministers cut their flesh and ate it.

sentences.zh: 壬申，嗣即皇帝位，大赦，改元永興。

translations.literal: On renshen, Si assumed the emperor's throne, proclaimed a general amnesty, and changed the era name to Yongxing.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen, Si took the throne, proclaimed a general amnesty, and changed the era name to Yongxing.

sentences.zh: 追尊劉貴人曰宣穆皇后，公卿先罷歸第不預朝政者，悉召用之。

translations.literal: He posthumously honored Lady Liu the Honored as Empress Xuanmu; all lords and ministers who had earlier been dismissed to their homes and excluded from court politics were summoned and employed.
translations.idiomatic: He posthumously honored Lady Liu as Empress Xuanmu; all lords and ministers who had been sent home and excluded from court were summoned back to office.

sentences.zh: 詔長孫嵩與北新侯安同、山陽侯奚斤、白馬侯崔宏、元城侯拓跋屈等八人坐止車門右，共聽朝政，時人謂之八公。

translations.literal: An edict made Changsun Song, An Tong the Marquis of Beixin, Xi Jin the Marquis of Shanyang, Cui Hong the Marquis of Baima, Tuoba Qu the Marquis of Yuancheng, and eight others in all sit to the right of the Chariot-Halting Gate to hear court politics together; people of the time called them the Eight Lords.
translations.idiomatic: An edict seated Changsun Song, An Tong Marquis of Beixin, Xi Jin Marquis of Shanyang, Cui Hong Marquis of Baima, Tuoba Qu Marquis of Yuancheng, and eight others to the right of the Chariot-Halting Gate to hear court affairs together; people called them the Eight Lords.

sentences.zh: 屈，磨渾之父也。

translations.literal: Qu was Mo Hun's father.
translations.idiomatic: Qu was Mo Hun's father.

sentences.zh: 嗣以尚書燕鳳逮事什翼犍使與都坐大官封懿等入侍講論，出議政事。

translations.literal: Si had Master of Writing Yan Feng, who had long served Shiyi Jian, enter attendance with Chief Director of the Great Office Feng Yi and others to lecture and discuss, and go out to deliberate on state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Si had Master of Writing Yan Feng, who had long served Shiyi Jian, enter attendance with Chief Director of the Great Office Feng Yi and others to lecture and debate, then go out to discuss state affairs.

sentences.zh: 以王洛兒、車路頭為散騎常侍，叔孫俊為衛將軍，拓跋磨渾為尚書，皆賜爵郡、縣公。

translations.literal: He made Wang Luo'er and Chelutou regular attendants, Shusun Jun defender general, Tuoba Mo Hun master of writing, and all enfeoffed them as dukes of commanderies and counties.
translations.idiomatic: He made Wang Luo'er and Chelutou regular attendants, Shusun Jun defender general, and Tuoba Mo Hun master of writing, and enfeoffed them all as commandery and county dukes.

sentences.zh: 嗣問舊臣為先帝所親信者為誰，王洛兒言李先。

translations.literal: Si asked which old ministers had been trusted by the late emperor; Wang Luo'er named Li Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Si asked which old ministers the late emperor had trusted; Wang Luo'er named Li Xian.

sentences.zh: 嗣召問先：「卿以何才何功為先帝所知？」

translations.literal: Si summoned and asked Xian: "By what talent and what merit were you known to the late emperor?"
translations.idiomatic: Si summoned Xian and asked, "By what talent and what merit did the late emperor know you?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣不才無功，但以忠直為先帝所知耳。」

translations.literal: He replied: "Your servant has no talent and no merit; I was known to the late emperor only through loyalty and straight dealing."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Your servant has no talent and no merit; the late emperor knew me only for loyalty and straight dealing."

sentences.zh: 詔以先為安東將軍，常宿於內，以備顧問。

translations.literal: An edict made Xian general who pacifies the east; he lodged constantly within the palace as a consultant at hand.
translations.idiomatic: An edict made him General Who Pacifies the East; he lodged constantly within the palace to be consulted.

sentences.zh: 朱提王悅，虔之子也，有罪，自疑懼。

translations.literal: Yue, Prince of Zhuti, was the son of Qian; he had committed offenses and suspected and feared for himself.
translations.idiomatic: Yue, Prince of Zhuti, was Qian's son; he had committed offenses and lived in fear.

sentences.zh: 閏十一月，丁亥，悅懷匕首入侍，將作亂。

translations.literal: In the intercalary eleventh month, on dinghai, Yue concealed a dagger in his bosom and entered attendance, intending to cause disorder.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary eleventh month, on dinghai, Yue hid a dagger in his robe and entered attendance, intending to rebel.

sentences.zh: 叔孫俊覺其舉止有異，引手掣之，索懷中，得匕首，遂殺之。

translations.literal: Shusun Jun noticed his manner was unusual, reached out and pulled him, searched his bosom, found the dagger, and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Shusun Jun noticed his manner was strange, grabbed him, searched his robe, found the dagger, and killed him.

sentences.zh: 十二月，乙巳，太白犯虛、危。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on yisi, Venus infringed on Xu and Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on yisi, Venus infringed on the Xu and Wei asterisms.

sentences.zh: 南燕靈台令張光勸南燕主超出降，超手殺之。

translations.literal: Zhang Guang, director of the observatory of Southern Yan, urged Southern Yan's ruler Murong Chao to surrender; Chao killed him with his own hand.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Guang, director of the observatory of Southern Yan, urged Southern Yan's ruler Murong Chao to surrender; Chao killed him with his own hand.

sentences.zh: 柔然侵魏。

translations.literal: The Rouran invaded Wei.
translations.idiomatic: The Rouran invaded Wei.

sentences.zh: 安皇帝庚義熙六年（

translations.literal: Emperor An, the sixth year of Yixi (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor An, the sixth year of Yixi (

sentences.zh: 庚戌，公元四一零年）

translations.literal: gengxu, AD 410)
