translations.idiomatic: gengxu, AD 410)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，甲寅朔，南燕主超登天門，朝群臣於城上。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on jiayin the new moon, Southern Yan's ruler Murong Chao ascended the Heavenly Gate and held court with his ministers atop the wall.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on the jiayin new moon, Southern Yan's ruler Murong Chao ascended the Heavenly Gate and held court with his ministers atop the wall.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，超與寵姬魏夫人登城，見晉兵之盛，握手對泣。

translations.literal: On yimao, Chao and his favored concubine Lady Wei ascended the wall, saw the strength of the Jin army, clasped hands, and wept facing each other.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao, Chao and his favored concubine Lady Wei went up on the wall, saw how strong the Jin army was, clasped hands, and wept together.

sentences.zh: 韓言卓諫曰：「陛下遭堙厄之運，正當努力自強以壯士民之志，而更為兒女子泣邪！」

translations.literal: Han Yanzhuo remonstrated, saying: "Your Majesty meets a time of buried calamity; you should exert yourself to strengthen resolve among officers and people—yet instead you weep like women and children!"
translations.idiomatic: Han Yanzhuo remonstrated, "Your Majesty faces a time of buried calamity; you should exert yourself to strengthen the resolve of officers and people—yet you weep like women and children!"

sentences.zh: 超拭目謝之。

translations.literal: Chao wiped his eyes and apologized.
translations.idiomatic: Chao wiped his eyes and apologized.

sentences.zh: 尚書令董銑勸超降，超怒，囚之。

translations.literal: Dong Xuan, master of writing, urged Chao to surrender; Chao was angry and imprisoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Master of Writing Dong Xuan urged Chao to surrender; Chao was furious and had him imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 魏長孫嵩將兵伐柔然。

translations.literal: Wei Changsun Song led troops against the Rouran.
translations.idiomatic: Changsun Song of Wei led troops against the Rouran.

sentences.zh: 魏主嗣以郡縣豪右多為民患，悉以優詔征之。

translations.literal: Emperor Si of Wei, because powerful local families in the commanderies and counties were often a pest to the people, summoned them all with gracious edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Si of Wei, because powerful local families in the commanderies and counties were often a pest to the people, summoned them all with gracious edicts.

sentences.zh: 民戀土不樂內徙，長吏逼遣之，於是無賴少年逃亡相聚，所在寇盜群起。

translations.literal: The people were attached to their lands and did not rejoice at moving inward; local officials forced them to depart; thereby worthless youths fled and gathered together, and bandit raids rose everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: The people were attached to their lands and did not wish to move inward; local officials forced them to go; worthless youths fled and banded together, and bandit raids broke out everywhere.

sentences.zh: 嗣引八公議之曰：「朕欲為民除蠹，而守宰不能綏撫，使之紛亂。

translations.literal: Si convened the Eight Lords to discuss it and said: "I wished to remove the vermin for the people, yet the prefects and magistrates could not soothe and settle them, and caused disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Si convened the Eight Lords and said, "I wished to rid the people of pests, yet the prefects and magistrates could not soothe them and caused disorder instead.

sentences.zh: 今犯者既眾，不可盡誅，吾欲大赦以安之，何如？」

translations.literal: Now the offenders are many and cannot all be executed; I wish to proclaim a general amnesty to settle them—what do you think?"
translations.idiomatic: Now the offenders are too many to execute all; I wish to proclaim a general amnesty to settle them—what do you think?"

sentences.zh: 元城侯屈曰：「民逃亡為盜，不罪而赦之，是為上者反求於下也，不如誅其首惡，赦其餘黨。」

translations.literal: Qu, Marquis of Yuancheng, said: "When the people flee and become bandits, to pardon without punishing is for those above to seek favor from those below; better to execute the chief evildoers and pardon the rest."
translations.idiomatic: Qu, Marquis of Yuancheng, said, "When people flee and turn bandit, to pardon without punishing is for those above to seek favor from those below; better to execute the ringleaders and pardon the rest."

sentences.zh: 崔宏曰：「聖王之御民，務在安之而已，不與之較勝負也。

translations.literal: Cui Hong said: "A sage king in governing the people seeks only to settle them—not to contest victory and defeat with them.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Hong said, "A sage king governs the people by settling them—not by contesting victory and defeat with them.

sentences.zh: 夫赦雖非正，可以行權。

translations.literal: A pardon, though not orthodox, may be used as expedient power.
translations.idiomatic: A pardon, though not orthodox, may be used as an expedient.

sentences.zh: 屈欲先誅後赦，要為兩不能去，曷若一赦而遂定乎！

translations.literal: Qu wishes first to execute and then pardon—in the end neither can be removed; why not one pardon and settle it at once!
translations.idiomatic: Qu wants to execute first and pardon after—in the end you cannot have both; why not one pardon and settle it at once!

sentences.zh: 赦而不從，誅未晚也。」

translations.literal: If after pardon they do not obey, execution will not be too late."
translations.idiomatic: If they do not obey after pardon, execution will not be too late."

sentences.zh: 嗣從之。

translations.literal: Si followed this advice.
translations.idiomatic: Si followed this advice.

sentences.zh: 二月，癸未朔，遣將軍於栗磾將騎一萬討不從命者，所向皆平。

translations.literal: In the second month, on guiwei the new moon, he sent General Yu Libi at the head of ten thousand horse to punish those who would not obey; wherever he went all was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the guiwei new moon, he sent General Yu Libi at the head of ten thousand horse to punish those who would not obey; wherever he went, all was pacified.

sentences.zh: 南燕賀賴盧、公孫五樓為地道出擊晉兵，不能卻。

translations.literal: Southern Yan's He Lu and Gongsun Wulou made a tunnel and sallied against the Jin army but could not drive them back.
translations.idiomatic: Southern Yan's He Lu and Gongsun Wulou dug a tunnel and sallied against the Jin army but could not drive them back.

sentences.zh: 城久閉，城中男女病腳弱者太半，出降者相繼。

translations.literal: The city had long been shut; more than half of men and women in the city were sick or lame in the legs; those who came out to surrender followed one after another.
translations.idiomatic: The city had long been shut; more than half the men and women inside were sick or lame; those who came out to surrender followed one after another.

sentences.zh: 超輦而登城，尚書悅壽說超曰：「今天助寇為虐，戰士調瘁，獨守窮城，絕望外援，天時人事亦可知矣。

translations.literal: Chao was carried in a carriage to ascend the wall; Yue Shou, master of writing, urged Chao, saying: "Today Heaven aids the invaders in their cruelty; the warriors are exhausted; you stand alone in a bankrupt city, with no hope of outside relief—the signs of Heaven and men alike may be read.
translations.idiomatic: Chao was carried in a carriage up onto the wall; Master of Writing Yue Shou urged him, "Today Heaven aids the invaders; the warriors are exhausted; you stand alone in a doomed city with no hope of outside relief—the signs of Heaven and men alike are clear.

sentences.zh: 苟歷數有終，堯、舜避位，陛下豈可不思變通之計乎！」

translations.literal: If the allotted span has its end, Yao and Shun yielded the throne—can Your Majesty not consider plans for adaptive change!"
translations.idiomatic: If the allotted span has its end, Yao and Shun yielded the throne—can Your Majesty not consider some adaptive plan!"

sentences.zh: 超歎曰：「廢興，命也。

translations.literal: Chao sighed and said: "Rise and fall are fate.
translations.idiomatic: Chao sighed and said, "Rise and fall are fate.

sentences.zh: 吾寧奮劍而死，不能銜璧而生！」

translations.literal: I would rather die with sword raised than live holding jade in surrender!"
translations.idiomatic: I would rather die with sword in hand than live holding jade in surrender!"

sentences.zh: 丁亥，劉裕悉眾攻城。

translations.literal: On dinghai, Liu Yu led all his forces to assault the city.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai, Liu Yu led all his forces to assault the city.

sentences.zh: 或曰：「今日往亡，不利行師。」

translations.literal: Someone said: "Today is wang wang—it is unfavorable to move troops."
translations.idiomatic: Someone said, "Today is wang wang—an inauspicious day for moving troops."

sentences.zh: 裕曰：「我往彼亡，何為不利！」

translations.literal: Yu said: "I go, they perish—what is unfavorable about that!"
translations.idiomatic: Yu said, "I go, they perish—what is unfavorable about that!"

sentences.zh: 四面急攻之。

translations.literal: They pressed the attack on all four sides.
translations.idiomatic: They pressed the attack on all four sides.

sentences.zh: 悅壽開門納晉師，超與左右數十騎逾城突圍出走，追獲之。

translations.literal: Yue Shou opened the gate and admitted the Jin army; Chao with several dozen horsemen of his entourage broke out over the wall and fled, but was pursued and captured.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Shou opened the gate and admitted the Jin army; Chao broke out over the wall with several dozen horsemen of his entourage, but was pursued and captured.

sentences.zh: 裕數以不降之罪，超神色自若，一無所言，惟以母托劉敬宣而已。

translations.literal: Yu repeatedly enumerated the crime of not surrendering; Chao's expression was calm, he said nothing at all, and only entrusted his mother to Liu Jingxuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yu repeatedly denounced him for not surrendering; Chao's expression was calm and he said nothing—only entrusting his mother to Liu Jingxuan.

sentences.zh: 裕忿廣固久不下，欲盡坑之，以妻女以賞將士。

translations.literal: Yu, vexed that Guanggu had long held out, wished to put the entire population to the sword and give wives and daughters as rewards to officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Yu, furious that Guanggu had held out so long, wished to slaughter the entire population and give wives and daughters as rewards to his officers and soldiers.

sentences.zh: 韓范諫曰：「晉室南遷，中原鼎沸，士民無援，強則附之，既為君臣，必須為之盡力。

translations.literal: Han Fan remonstrated, saying: "The Jin house moved south; the central plains seethed; scholars and people had no aid; the strong attached themselves—once subject and ruler, they had to serve with full effort.
translations.idiomatic: Han Fan remonstrated, "The Jin house moved south; the central plains seethed; scholars and people had no aid; the strong attached themselves—and once subject and ruler, they had to serve with full effort.

sentences.zh: 彼皆衣冠舊族，先帝遺民；

translations.literal: They were all old families of the gentry, surviving people of the former emperors;
translations.idiomatic: They were all old gentry families, surviving people of the former emperors;

sentences.zh: 今王師吊伐而盡坑之，使安所歸乎！

translations.literal: now the royal army comes in punitive relief yet would slaughter them all—where would they turn!
translations.idiomatic: now the royal army comes in punitive relief yet would slaughter them all—where would they turn!

sentences.zh: 竊恐西北之人無復來蘇之望矣。」

translations.literal: I fear privately that the people of the northwest would have no further hope of revival."
translations.idiomatic: I fear the people of the northwest would have no further hope of revival."

sentences.zh: 裕改容謝之，然猶斬王公以下三千人，沒入家口萬餘，夷其城隍，送超詣建康，斬之。

translations.literal: Yu changed expression and apologized, yet still beheaded three thousand from kings and dukes downward, confiscated more than ten thousand household members, razed the walls and moat, sent Chao to Jiankang, and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Yu changed expression and apologized, yet still executed three thousand from kings and dukes downward, confiscated more than ten thousand household members, razed the walls and moat, sent Chao to Jiankang, and executed him.

sentences.zh: 臣光曰：晉自濟江以來，威靈不競，戎狄橫騖，虎噬中原。

translations.literal: Master Guang said: Since Jin crossed the river, its majesty and power have not competed; Rong and Di rampaged freely; tigers devoured the central plains.
translations.idiomatic: Master Guang said: Since Jin crossed the river, its majesty and power have waned; Rong and Di rampaged freely; tigers devoured the central plains.

sentences.zh: 劉裕始勸王師剪平東夏，不於此際旌禮賢俊，慰撫疲民，宣愷悌之風，滌殘穢之政，使群士向風，遺黎企踵，而更恣行屠戮以快忿心。

translations.literal: When Liu Yu first urged the royal army to cut down and pacify the eastern Xia, he did not at this juncture honor worthy men, comfort the exhausted people, proclaim a kindly forbearance, wash away corrupt policy, make the gentry turn toward the wind and the surviving masses raise their heels in hope—instead he wantonly slaughtered to satisfy wrath.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yu first urged the royal army to cut down and pacify the eastern Xia, he did not at this juncture honor worthy men, comfort the exhausted people, proclaim a spirit of kindness and forbearance, and wash away corrupt policy so the gentry would turn toward him and the surviving masses raise their heels in hope—instead he wantonly slaughtered to satisfy his wrath.

sentences.zh: 跡其施設，曾苻、姚之不如，宜其不能蕩壹四海，成美大之業，豈非雖有智勇而無仁義使之然哉！

translations.literal: Tracing his measures, he did not even match Fu and Yao; it is fitting he could not sweep unity across the four seas and accomplish a great and beautiful enterprise—is it not that though he had wisdom and courage, lacking benevolence and righteousness made it so!
translations.idiomatic: Tracing his measures, he did not even match Fu Jian and Yao Xing; it is fitting he could not sweep unity across the four seas and accomplish a great enterprise—is it not that though he had wisdom and courage, lacking benevolence and righteousness made it so!

sentences.zh: 初，徐道覆聞劉裕北伐，勸盧循乘虛襲建康，循不從。

translations.literal: Earlier, Xu Daofu heard Liu Yu was campaigning north and urged Lu Xun to exploit the opening and strike Jiankang; Xun would not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Xu Daofu heard Liu Yu was campaigning north and urged Lu Xun to exploit the opening and strike Jiankang; Xun would not listen.

sentences.zh: 道覆自至番禺說循曰：「本住嶺外，豈以理極於此，傳之子孫邪？

translations.literal: Daofu himself went to Panyu and said to Xun: "We originally dwelt beyond the ranges—do you think reason reaches this point and passes to sons and grandsons?
translations.idiomatic: Daofu himself went to Panyu and said to Xun, "We originally dwelt beyond the ranges—do you think reason reaches this point and passes to sons and grandsons?

sentences.zh: 正以劉裕難與為敵故也。

translations.literal: It is precisely because Liu Yu is hard to match as an enemy.
translations.idiomatic: It is precisely because Liu Yu is hard to match as an enemy.

sentences.zh: 今裕頓兵堅城之下，未有還期，我以此思歸死士掩擊何、劉之徒，如反掌耳。

translations.literal: Now Yu's army is stalled beneath stout walls with no date of return; with this I would gather home-yearning warriors willing to die and strike He and Liu—it would be like turning the palm.
translations.idiomatic: Now Yu's army is stalled beneath stout walls with no date of return; with this I would gather home-yearning warriors willing to die and strike He and Liu—it would be like turning the palm.

sentences.zh: 不乘此機，而苟求一日之安，朝廷常以君為腹心之疾；

translations.literal: If you do not seize this opportunity but seek only a day's peace, the court constantly treats you as a disease of the heart and belly;
translations.idiomatic: If you do not seize this opportunity but seek only a day's peace, the court constantly treats you as a disease of the heart and belly;

sentences.zh: 若裕平齊之後，息甲歲餘，以璽書征君，裕自將屯豫章，遣諸將帥銳師過嶺，雖復以將軍之神武，恐必不能當也。

translations.literal: If Yu pacifies Qi and then rests the army for more than a year, sends an imperial seal letter to summon you, personally leads troops to encamp at Yuzhang, and dispatches generals with crack forces across the ranges—even with your divine martial prowess, I fear you surely could not withstand him.
translations.idiomatic: If Yu pacifies Qi and then rests the army for more than a year, sends an imperial summons, personally encamps at Yuzhang, and dispatches generals with crack troops across the ranges—even with your martial prowess, I fear you could not withstand him.

sentences.zh: 今日之機，萬不可失。

translations.literal: Today's opportunity must on no account be lost.
translations.idiomatic: Today's opportunity must not be missed.

sentences.zh: 若先克建康，傾其根蒂。

translations.literal: If we first take Jiankang, we will overturn its roots and foundation.
translations.idiomatic: If we take Jiankang first, we will uproot the dynasty itself.

sentences.zh: 裕雖南還，無能為也。

translations.literal: Though Yu returns south, he will be unable to act.
translations.idiomatic: Even if Yu returns south, he will be powerless.

sentences.zh: 君若不同，便當帥始興之眾直指尋陽。」

translations.literal: If you do not agree, I shall lead the masses of Shixing straight against Xunyang."
translations.idiomatic: If you will not agree, I shall lead the Shixing forces straight against Xunyang."

sentences.zh: 循甚不樂此舉，而無以奪其計，乃從之。

translations.literal: Xun was very displeased with this plan, but had no way to override it, and so followed along.
translations.idiomatic: Xun was deeply unhappy with the plan, but could not talk him out of it, and so went along.

sentences.zh: 初，道覆使人伐船材於南康山，至始興，賤賣之，居人爭市之，船材大積而人不疑，至是，悉取以裝艦，旬日而辦。

translations.literal: Earlier, Daofu had men cut ship timber on Mount Nankang; when it reached Shixing, he sold it cheaply, and the residents competed to buy it. Ship timber piled up greatly yet no one suspected; at this time he took it all to fit out warships, and within ten days it was done.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Daofu had timber cut for ships on Mount Nankang; when it reached Shixing, he sold it cheaply, and locals snapped it up. Timber piled up without arousing suspicion; now he took it all to build warships, and within ten days the fleet was ready.

sentences.zh: 循自始興寇長沙，道覆寇南康、廬陵、豫章，諸守相皆委任奔走。

translations.literal: Xun himself raided Changsha from Shixing; Daofu raided Nankang, Luling, and Yuzhang; all the prefects and chancellors abandoned their posts and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Xun raided Changsha from Shixing while Daofu struck Nankang, Luling, and Yuzhang; prefects and chancellors everywhere abandoned their posts and fled.

sentences.zh: 道覆順流而下，舟械甚盛。

translations.literal: Daofu went downstream; his boats and weapons were very grand.
translations.idiomatic: Daofu sailed downstream with an imposing fleet.

sentences.zh: 時克燕之問未至，朝廷急征劉裕。

translations.literal: At this time word that Yan had been taken had not yet arrived; the court urgently summoned Liu Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Word that Yan had fallen had not yet arrived when the court urgently recalled Liu Yu.

sentences.zh: 裕方議留鎮下邳，經營司、雍，會得詔書，乃以韓范為都督八郡軍事、燕郡太守，封融為勃海太守，檀韶為琅邪太守，戊申，引兵還。

translations.literal: Yu was just discussing staying to garrison Xiapi and managing Si and Yong provinces when he received an imperial edict; he then made Han Fan commander of military affairs for eight commanderies and governor of Yan commandery, Feng Rong governor of Bohai, and Tan Shao governor of Langye; on wushen he led his troops back.
translations.idiomatic: Yu had been planning to stay and garrison Xiapi while securing Si and Yong when an edict arrived; he appointed Han Fan to command military affairs in eight commanderies and govern Yan, Feng Rong to govern Bohai, and Tan Shao to govern Langye, then on wushen marched his army home.

sentences.zh: 韶，祗之兄也。

translations.literal: Shao was the elder brother of Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Shao was Zhi's elder brother.

sentences.zh: 久之，劉穆之稱范、融謀反，皆殺之。

translations.literal: After some time, Liu Muzhi claimed Fan and Rong were plotting rebellion, and both were killed.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, Liu Muzhi accused Fan and Rong of plotting rebellion, and both were executed.

sentences.zh: 安成忠肅公何無忌自尋陽引兵拒盧循。

translations.literal: Duke Zhongsu of Ancheng, He Wuji, led troops from Xunyang to resist Lu Xun.
translations.idiomatic: He Wuji, Duke Zhongsu of Ancheng, led troops from Xunyang to resist Lu Xun.

sentences.zh: 長史鄧潛之諫曰：「國家安危，在此一舉。

translations.literal: Chief clerk Deng Qianzhi remonstrated, saying, "The safety or peril of the state hangs on this one move.
translations.idiomatic: Chief clerk Deng Qianzhi remonstrated, "The fate of the state hangs on this one move.

sentences.zh: 聞循兵艦大盛。

translations.literal: I hear Xun's warships are very strong.
translations.idiomatic: I hear Xun's fleet is formidable.

sentences.zh: 勢居上流，宜決南塘，守二城以待之，彼必不敢捨我遠下。

translations.literal: Their position is upstream; we should breach the Nantang dyke, hold the two cities and wait for them—they surely will not dare leave us and go far downstream.
translations.idiomatic: They hold the upstream advantage; we should breach the Nantang dyke, hold the two cities, and wait—they will not dare pass us by and sail on.

sentences.zh: 蓄力養銳，俟其疲老，然後擊之，此萬全之策也。

translations.literal: Store strength and nurture sharpness, wait until they are weary and aged, then strike—this is a strategy of complete safety.
translations.idiomatic: Conserve our strength, wait until they are worn down, then strike—this is the safest course.

sentences.zh: 今決成敗於一戰，萬一失利，悔將無及！」

translations.literal: Now to decide victory and defeat in a single battle—if by any chance we lose, regret will come too late!"
translations.idiomatic: To stake everything on one battle—if we lose, it will be too late for regret!"

sentences.zh: 參軍殷闡曰：「循所將之眾皆三吳舊賊，百戰餘勇，始興溪子，拳捷善鬥，未易輕也。

translations.literal: Army aide Yin Kan said, "The troops Xun leads are all old bandits of the Three Wu, veterans of a hundred battles with remaining courage; the stream lads of Shixing are quick with fists and skilled at fighting—not easily to be treated lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Army aide Yin Kan said, "The men Xun leads are old Three Wu rebels, battle-hardened veterans; the hill folk of Shixing are quick and fierce fighters—not to be underestimated.

sentences.zh: 將軍宜留屯豫章，徵兵屬城，兵至合戰，未為晚也。

translations.literal: The general should stay encamped at Yuzhang, summon troops from subordinate cities, and when the soldiers arrive join battle—it will not be too late.
translations.idiomatic: You should hold Yuzhang, summon troops from the surrounding cities, and fight when they arrive—it will not be too late.

sentences.zh: 若以此眾輕進，殆必有悔。」

translations.literal: If with these troops you advance lightly, there will likely be regret."
translations.idiomatic: If you advance rashly with this force, you will surely regret it."

sentences.zh: 無忌不聽。

translations.literal: Wuji would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Wuji refused to listen.

sentences.zh: 三月，壬申，與徐道覆遇於豫章，賊令強弩數百登西岸小山邀射之。

translations.literal: In the third month, on renshen, he met Xu Daofu at Yuzhang; the rebels had several hundred strong crossbows ascend a small hill on the west bank to intercept and shoot at them.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on renshen, he met Xu Daofu at Yuzhang; the rebels posted several hundred crossbowmen on a hill on the west bank to rake his force with arrows.

sentences.zh: 會西風暴急，飄無忌所乘小艦向東岸，賊乘風以大艦逼之，眾遂奔潰。

translations.literal: Just then a violent west wind arose and blew the small vessel Wuji was aboard toward the east bank; the rebels used the wind to press him with large ships, and the army fled in rout.
translations.idiomatic: A violent west wind then blew Wuji's small vessel toward the east bank; the rebels used the wind to close with their large ships, and his force broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 無忌厲聲曰：「取我蘇武節來！」

translations.literal: Wuji cried out in a harsh voice, "Bring me my Su Wu staff!"
translations.idiomatic: Wuji shouted, "Bring me my Su Wu staff!"

sentences.zh: 節至，執以督戰。

translations.literal: When the staff arrived, he grasped it to direct the battle.
translations.idiomatic: When the staff was brought, he seized it and rallied the fight.

sentences.zh: 賊眾雲集，無忌辭色無撓，握節而死。

translations.literal: Rebel masses gathered like clouds; Wuji's words and expression did not waver, and he died grasping the staff.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel forces swarmed around him; Wuji did not flinch, and died still gripping the staff.

sentences.zh: 於是中外震駭，朝議欲奉乘輿北走就劉裕；

translations.literal: Thereupon court and countryside were shaken with terror; court deliberation wished to escort the imperial carriage north to join Liu Yu;
translations.idiomatic: Court and countryside were shaken; some at court proposed escorting the emperor north to Liu Yu;

sentences.zh: 既而知賊未至，乃止。

translations.literal: then, learning the rebels had not yet arrived, they stopped.
translations.idiomatic: then, learning the rebels had not yet arrived, they dropped the idea.

sentences.zh: 西秦王乾歸攻秦金城郡，拔之。

translations.literal: Qifu Gangui, king of Western Qin, attacked Jincheng commandery of Qin and took it.
translations.idiomatic: Qifu Gangui, king of Western Qin, attacked Qin's Jincheng commandery and captured it.

sentences.zh: 夏王勃勃遣尚書朝金纂攻平涼。

translations.literal: Helian Bobo, king of Xia, sent the master of writing Chao Jinzuan to attack Pingliang.
translations.idiomatic: Helian Bobo, king of Xia, sent master of writing Chao Jinzuan to attack Pingliang.

sentences.zh: 秦王興救平涼，擊金纂，殺之。

translations.literal: Yao Xing, king of Qin, rescued Pingliang, struck Jinzuan, and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing, king of Qin, marched to relieve Pingliang, defeated Jinzuan, and killed him.

sentences.zh: 勃勃又遣兄子左將軍羅提攻拔定陽，坑將士四千餘人。

translations.literal: Bobo again sent his elder brother's son, Left General Luo Ti, to attack and take Dingyang, and buried alive more than four thousand officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Bobo then sent his nephew, Left General Luo Ti, to capture Dingyang and buried alive more than four thousand officers and soldiers.

sentences.zh: 秦將曹熾、曹雲、王肆佛等各將數千亡內徙，興處之湟山及陳倉。

translations.literal: Qin generals Cao Chi, Cao Yun, Wang Sifo, and others each led several thousand men in flight inward; Xing settled them at Huangshan and Chencang.
translations.idiomatic: Qin generals Cao Chi, Cao Yun, Wang Sifo, and others each fled inland with several thousand men; Xing resettled them at Huangshan and Chencang.

sentences.zh: 勃勃寇隴右，破白崖堡，遂趣清水，略陽太守姚壽都棄城走，勃勃徙其民萬六千戶於大城。

translations.literal: Bobo raided Longyou, broke Baicheng Fort, then pressed toward Qingshui; Yao Shoudu, governor of Lueyang, abandoned the city and fled; Bobo moved sixteen thousand of its households to Dacheng.
translations.idiomatic: Bobo raided Longyou, took Baicheng Fort, and pressed on toward Qingshui; Yao Shoudu, governor of Lueyang, abandoned the city and fled; Bobo relocated sixteen thousand households to Dacheng.

sentences.zh: 興自安定追之，至壽渠川，不及而還。

translations.literal: Xing pursued from Anding as far as Shouqu Stream, failed to catch up, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Xing pursued from Anding as far as Shouqu Stream but could not overtake him and turned back.

sentences.zh: 初，南涼王辱檀遣左將軍枯木等伐沮渠蒙遜，掠臨松千餘戶而還。

translations.literal: Earlier, Juqu Rouran, king of Southern Liang, sent Left General Kumu and others to attack Juqu Mengxun, plundered more than a thousand households at Linsong, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Juqu Rouran, king of Southern Liang, sent Left General Kumu and others against Juqu Mengxun, plundered more than a thousand households at Linsong, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜伐南涼，至顯美，徙數千戶而去。

translations.literal: Mengxun attacked Southern Liang, reached Xianmei, moved off several thousand households, and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun struck Southern Liang, reached Xianmei, relocated several thousand households, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 南涼太尉俱延復伐蒙遜，大敗而歸。

translations.literal: Ju Yan, grand marshal of Southern Liang, again attacked Mengxun and returned after a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Ju Yan, grand marshal of Southern Liang, attacked Mengxun again and returned in defeat.

sentences.zh: 是月，辱檀自將五萬騎伐蒙遜，戰於窮泉，辱檀大敗，單馬奔還。

translations.literal: That month, Rouran personally led fifty thousand cavalry against Mengxun; they fought at Qiongquan; Rouran was greatly defeated and fled back alone on horseback.
translations.idiomatic: That month, Rouran personally led fifty thousand cavalry against Mengxun; at Qiongquan he was routed and fled back alone on horseback.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜乘勝進圍姑臧，姑臧人懲王鐘之誅，皆驚潰，夷、夏萬餘戶降於蒙遜。

translations.literal: Mengxun pressed the victory and advanced to besiege Guzang; the people of Guzang, mindful of Wang Zhong's execution, all fled in panic and collapse; more than ten thousand households of barbarians and Chinese surrendered to Mengxun.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun pressed his advantage and besieged Guzang; the people of Guzang, still mindful of Wang Zhong's execution, panicked and fled, and more than ten thousand barbarian and Chinese households surrendered to Mengxun.

sentences.zh: 辱檀懼，遣司隸校尉敬歸及子佗為質於蒙遜以請和，蒙遜許之。

translations.literal: Rouran was afraid and sent Director of Retainers Jing Gui and his son Tuo as hostages to Mengxun to sue for peace; Mengxun agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing the worst, Rouran sent director of retainers Jing Gui and his son Tuo as hostages to Mengxun to sue for peace, and Mengxun agreed.

sentences.zh: 歸至胡坑，逃還，佗為追兵所執，蒙遜徙其眾八千餘戶而去。

translations.literal: Gui reached Hukeng and fled back; Tuo was seized by pursuing troops; Mengxun moved off more than eight thousand of their people and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Gui escaped at Hukeng and fled home; Tuo was captured by pursuers; Mengxun relocated more than eight thousand of their people and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 右衛將軍折掘奇鎮據石驢山以叛。

translations.literal: Right Guard General Zheju Qizhen seized Shilü Mountain and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Right Guard General Zheju Qizhen seized Mount Shilü and rebelled.

sentences.zh: 辱檀畏蒙孫之逼，且懼嶺南為奇鎮所據，乃遷於樂都，留大司農成公緒守姑臧。

translations.literal: Rouran feared Mengxun's pressure and also feared that south of the ranges Qizhen would hold the territory, so he moved to Ledu and left Grand Minister of Agriculture Cheng Gongxu to guard Guzang.
translations.idiomatic: Rouran feared Mengxun's pressure and also that Qizhen would hold the lands south of the ranges, so he moved his seat to Ledu and left grand minister of agriculture Cheng Gongxu to hold Guzang.

sentences.zh: 辱檀才出城，魏安人侯諶等閉門作亂，收合三千餘家，據南城，推焦朗為大都督、龍驤大將軍，諶自稱涼州刺史，降於蒙遜。

translations.literal: Rouran had barely left the city when Wei'an men Hou Chen and others closed the gates and raised rebellion, gathered more than three thousand households, held the south city, made Jiao Lang grand commander and Dragon Cavalry General, and Chen styled himself inspector of Liang and surrendered to Mengxun.
translations.idiomatic: Rouran had barely left the city when Hou Chen of Wei'an and others shut the gates in revolt, rallied more than three thousand households, seized the south city, made Jiao Lang grand commander and dragon cavalry general, styled himself inspector of Liang, and surrendered to Mengxun.

sentences.zh: 劉裕至下邳，以船載輜重，自帥精銳步歸。

translations.literal: Liu Yu reached Xiapi, loaded baggage and supplies on ships, and personally led picked troops home on foot.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu reached Xiapi, sent baggage and supplies by ship, and marched home at the head of his elite troops.

sentences.zh: 至山陽，聞何無忌敗死，慮京邑失守，卷甲兼行，與數十人至淮上，問行人以朝廷消息，行人曰：「賊尚未至，劉公若還，便無所憂。」

translations.literal: When he reached Shanyang, he heard He Wuji had been defeated and killed; fearing the capital district would fall, he rolled up his armor and marched day and night; with several dozen men he reached the Huai and asked travelers for news from court; a traveler said, "The rebels have not yet arrived; if Lord Liu returns, there will be nothing to worry about."
translations.idiomatic: At Shanyang he learned that He Wuji had been defeated and killed; fearing the capital would fall, he forced the march day and night; with a few dozen men he reached the Huai and asked passersby for news from court; one said, "The rebels have not arrived yet; if Lord Liu returns, there will be nothing to fear."

sentences.zh: 裕大喜。

translations.literal: Yu was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was greatly relieved.

sentences.zh: 將濟江，風急，眾鹹難之。

translations.literal: About to cross the river, the wind was fierce and the crowd all found it difficult.
translations.idiomatic: As he was about to cross the river, the wind blew hard and his men all objected.

sentences.zh: 裕曰：「若天命助國，風當自息；

translations.literal: Yu said, "If Heaven's mandate aids the state, the wind should calm of itself;
translations.idiomatic: Yu said, "If Heaven favors the state, the wind will die down on its own;

sentences.zh: 若其不然，覆溺何害！」

translations.literal: if it is not so, what harm in capsizing and drowning!"
translations.idiomatic: if not, what harm is there in drowning!"

sentences.zh: 即命登舟，舟移而風止。

translations.literal: He at once ordered them aboard; as the boat moved, the wind stopped.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered them aboard at once; as the boat put out, the wind fell.

sentences.zh: 過江，至京口，眾乃大安。

translations.literal: Crossing the river, he reached Jingkou, and the masses were greatly reassured.
translations.idiomatic: After crossing the river he reached Jingkou, and the people were greatly reassured.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，癸未，裕至建康。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on guiwei, Yu reached Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on guiwei, Yu reached Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 以江州覆沒，表送章綬，詔不許。

translations.literal: Because Jiang province had been overrun, he submitted a memorial returning his seal and cord; an edict did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Because Jiang province had fallen, he memorialized the throne offering to surrender his seal and cord; the edict refused.

sentences.zh: 青州刺史諸葛長民、兗州刺史劉籓、并州刺史劉道憐各將兵入衛逮康。

translations.literal: Zhuge Changmin, inspector of Qing province, Liu Fan, inspector of Yan province, and Liu Daolian, inspector of Bing province, each led troops to enter and guard Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Changmin, inspector of Qing, Liu Fan, inspector of Yan, and Liu Daolian, inspector of Bing, each led troops to defend Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 籓，兗州刺史毅之從弟也。

translations.literal: Fan was a younger cousin of Liu Yi, inspector of Yan province.
translations.idiomatic: Fan was a younger cousin of Liu Yi, inspector of Yan.

sentences.zh: 毅聞盧循之寇，將拒之，而疾作；

translations.literal: Yi heard of Lu Xun's raid and was about to resist it, but illness struck;
translations.idiomatic: When Yi heard of Lu Xun's invasion, he prepared to resist, but fell ill;

sentences.zh: 既瘳，將行。

translations.literal: once recovered, he was about to set out.
translations.idiomatic: once he recovered, he prepared to march.

sentences.zh: 劉裕遺毅書曰：「吾往習擊妖賊，曉其變態。

translations.literal: Liu Yu sent Yi a letter saying, "I am accustomed from past experience to striking demonic rebels and understand their shifts.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu wrote to Yi, "I have fought these rebel bands before and know their ways.

sentences.zh: 賊新獲奸利，其鋒不可輕。

translations.literal: The rebels have newly gained illicit profit; their edge must not be treated lightly.
translations.idiomatic: They have just won an easy victory; their momentum must not be underestimated.

sentences.zh: 今修船垂畢，當與弟同舉。

translations.literal: Now ship repairs are nearly finished; I shall act together with you, my younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Our ships are nearly ready; we should strike together.

sentences.zh: 克平之日，上流之任，皆以相委。」

translations.literal: On the day of victory and pacification, the duties of the upper reaches will all be entrusted to you."
translations.idiomatic: When victory is won, I will entrust the upper Yangzi command to you."

sentences.zh: 又遣劉籓往諭止之。

translations.literal: He also sent Liu Fan to instruct and stop him.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent Liu Fan to dissuade him.

sentences.zh: 毅怒，謂籓曰：「往以一時之功相推耳，汝便謂我真不及劉裕邪！」

translations.literal: Yi was angry and said to Fan, "In the past you promoted me for a moment's achievement—do you really think I am truly no match for Liu Yu!"
translations.idiomatic: Yi was furious and said to Fan, "You once praised me for a single victory—do you really think I am no match for Liu Yu!"

sentences.zh: 投書於地，帥舟師二萬發姑孰。

translations.literal: He threw the letter to the ground and led twenty thousand river troops from Gudu.
translations.idiomatic: He threw the letter down and sailed from Gudu with twenty thousand men.

sentences.zh: 循之初入寇也，使徐道覆向尋陽，循自將攻湘中諸郡。

translations.literal: When Xun first entered in raid, he sent Xu Daofu toward Xunyang while he personally led the attack on the commanderies of central Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: When Xun first invaded, he sent Xu Daofu toward Xunyang while he personally attacked the commanderies of central Hunan.

sentences.zh: 荊州刺史劉道規遣軍逆戰，敗於長沙。

translations.literal: Liu Daogui, inspector of Jing province, sent troops to meet them in battle and was defeated at Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Daogui, inspector of Jing, sent troops to intercept them and was defeated at Changsha.

sentences.zh: 循進至巴陵，將向江陵。

translations.literal: Xun advanced to Baling and was about to move toward Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: Xun advanced to Baling and prepared to march on Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 徐道覆聞毅將至，馳使報循曰：「毅兵甚盛，成敗之事，系之於此，宜並力摧之。

translations.literal: Xu Daofu heard Yi was about to arrive and sent a fast messenger to report to Xun, saying, "Yi's troops are very strong; the matter of victory or defeat hangs on this—we should combine strength to crush him.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Daofu heard Yi was approaching and sent an urgent message to Xun: "Yi's force is formidable; victory or defeat hangs on this—we must combine and crush him.

sentences.zh: 若此克捷，江陵不足憂也。」

translations.literal: If we gain victory here, Jiangling need not be worried over."
translations.idiomatic: If we win here, Jiangling will no longer matter."

sentences.zh: 循即日發巴陵，與道覆合兵而下。

translations.literal: Xun that same day set out from Baling, joined forces with Daofu, and went downstream.
translations.idiomatic: Xun left Baling that same day, joined Daofu, and sailed downstream.

sentences.zh: 五月，戊午，毅與循戰於桑落洲，毅兵大敗，棄船，以數百人步走，餘眾皆為循所虜，所棄輜重山積。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on wuwu, Yi fought Xun at Sangluo Isle; Yi's army was greatly defeated; he abandoned his ships and fled on foot with several hundred men; the rest were all captured by Xun; abandoned baggage and supplies piled like mountains.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on wuwu, Yi fought Xun at Sangluo Isle and was routed; he abandoned his ships and fled on foot with a few hundred men while the rest were captured; abandoned supplies piled like hills.

sentences.zh: 初，循至尋陽，聞裕已還，猶不信；

translations.literal: Earlier, when Xun reached Xunyang, he heard Yu had already returned but still did not believe it;
translations.idiomatic: When Xun reached Xunyang, he heard Yu had returned but did not believe it;

sentences.zh: 既破毅，乃得審問，與其黨相視失色。

translations.literal: after defeating Yi, he then obtained verified inquiry; he and his partisans looked at one another and lost color.
translations.idiomatic: only after defeating Yi did he learn it was true; he and his followers looked at one another in dismay.

sentences.zh: 循欲退還尋陽，攻取江陵，據二州以抗朝廷。

translations.literal: Xun wished to withdraw to Xunyang, take Jiangling, and hold the two provinces to resist the court.
translations.idiomatic: Xun wanted to fall back to Xunyang, seize Jiangling, and hold the two provinces against the court.

sentences.zh: 道覆謂宜乘勝徑進，固爭之。

translations.literal: Daofu said they should ride the victory and press straight forward, and argued it firmly.
translations.idiomatic: Daofu argued they should press the victory and advance directly, and pressed the point hard.

sentences.zh: 循猶豫累日，乃從之。

translations.literal: Xun hesitated for several days, then followed him.
translations.idiomatic: Xun hesitated for days, then agreed.

sentences.zh: 己未，大赦。

translations.literal: On jiwei, a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei, a general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 裕募人為兵，賞之同京口赴義之科。

translations.literal: Yu recruited men as soldiers and rewarded them on the same scale as the Jingkou righteous rising.
translations.idiomatic: Yu recruited soldiers and offered rewards on the same terms as the Jingkou uprising.

sentences.zh: 發民治石頭城。

translations.literal: He mobilized the people to repair Stone City.
translations.idiomatic: He mobilized civilians to repair Stone City.

sentences.zh: 議者謂宜分兵守諸津要，裕曰：「賊眾我寡，若分兵屯守，則測人虛實；

translations.literal: Those deliberating said troops should be divided to guard the key crossings; Yu said, "The rebels are many and we are few; if we divide troops to garrison posts, they will probe our strength and weakness;
translations.idiomatic: Some argued for dividing forces to hold the key crossings; Yu said, "The enemy outnumbers us; if we split up to garrison posts, they will probe our strength;

sentences.zh: 且一處失利，則沮三軍之心。

translations.literal: moreover, if one place is lost, it will damp the hearts of the three armies.
translations.idiomatic: and if one post falls, the whole army's morale will collapse.

sentences.zh: 今聚眾石頭，隨宜應赴，既令彼無以測多少，又於眾力不分。

translations.literal: Now gather the masses at Stone City and respond as circumstances require—this both keeps them from measuring how many we are and keeps our collective strength undivided.
translations.idiomatic: Better to concentrate at Stone City and respond wherever needed—this hides our numbers and keeps our strength intact.

sentences.zh: 若徒旅轉集，徐更論之耳。」

translations.literal: If stragglers keep gathering, we can discuss it again at leisure."
translations.idiomatic: If more troops keep arriving, we can reconsider then."

sentences.zh: 朝廷聞劉毅敗，人情恟懼。

translations.literal: The court heard Liu Yi had been defeated; popular sentiment was alarmed and fearful.
translations.idiomatic: When the court learned Liu Yi had been defeated, panic spread.

sentences.zh: 時北師始還，將士多創病，建康戰士不盈數千。

translations.literal: At this time the northern army had just returned; officers and soldiers were mostly wounded and ill; Jiankang's fighting men numbered fewer than several thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The northern army had just returned; many officers and soldiers were wounded or sick; Jiankang had fewer than a few thousand fit fighters.

sentences.zh: 循既克二鎮，戰士十餘萬，舟車百里不絕，樓船高十二丈，敗還者爭言其強盛。

translations.literal: Xun having taken the two garrison towns, his fighting men numbered more than a hundred thousand; boats and wagons stretched unbroken for a hundred li; tower ships stood twelve zhang high; those who fled back competed in describing their strength.
translations.idiomatic: Xun had taken two garrison towns and fielded more than a hundred thousand fighters; his fleet stretched for a hundred li without a break, with tower ships twelve zhang high; refugees competed to describe his might.

sentences.zh: 孟昶、諸葛長民欲奉乘輿過江，裕不聽。

translations.literal: Meng Chang and Zhuge Changmin wished to escort the imperial carriage across the river; Yu would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Chang and Zhuge Changmin wanted to move the emperor south across the river; Yu refused.

sentences.zh: 初，何無忌、劉毅之南討也，昶策其必敗，已而果然。

translations.literal: Earlier, when He Wuji and Liu Yi marched south to attack, Chang had calculated they would surely be defeated, and soon it was indeed so.
translations.idiomatic: When He Wuji and Liu Yi marched south, Chang had predicted defeat, and he was proved right.

sentences.zh: 至是，又謂裕必不能抗循，眾頗信之。

translations.literal: At this time he again said Yu surely could not resist Xun, and many quite believed him.
translations.idiomatic: Now he said Yu could not possibly stand against Xun, and many believed him.

sentences.zh: 惟龍驤將軍東海虞丘進廷折昶等，以為不然。

translations.literal: Only Dragon Cavalry General Yuqiu Jinting of Donghai rebutted Chang and the others in court, holding it was not so.
translations.idiomatic: Only Dragon Cavalry General Yuqiu Jinting of Donghai argued against Chang and the others in open court.

sentences.zh: 中兵參軍王仲德言於裕曰：「明公命世作輔，新建大功，威震六合，妖賊乘虛入寇，既聞凱還，自當奔潰。

translations.literal: Central Army aide Wang Zhongde said to Yu, "My lord, born to the age as chief minister, has newly achieved great merit and whose awe shakes the six directions; demonic rebels exploit a gap to enter in raid—once they hear of triumphant return, they should naturally flee in rout.
translations.idiomatic: Central army aide Wang Zhongde said to Yu, "My lord was born to serve the age, has just won great victories, and your fame shakes the realm; these rebels invaded while we were exposed—once they hear you have returned in triumph, they should break and flee.

sentences.zh: 若先自遁逃，則勢同匹夫，匹夫號令，何以威物！

translations.literal: If you first flee yourself, then your position is the same as a common man's—what common man's orders can awe others!
translations.idiomatic: If you flee first, you are no more than a common man—and what common man can command awe!

sentences.zh: 此謀若立，請從此辭。」

translations.literal: If this plan is adopted, I ask to take my leave from here."
translations.idiomatic: If you adopt this plan, I must resign."

sentences.zh: 裕甚悅。

translations.literal: Yu was very pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 昶固請不已，裕曰：「今重鎮外傾，強寇內逼，人情危駭，莫有固志；

translations.literal: Chang pressed his request without cease; Yu said, "Now key garrison towns lean outward in collapse, a strong foe presses inward, popular sentiment is terrified and shaken, and no one has a firm will;
translations.idiomatic: Chang kept pressing his case; Yu said, "Our outer defenses have fallen, a powerful enemy presses inward, the people are terrified, and no one has a firm heart;

sentences.zh: 若一旦遷動，便自土崩瓦解，江北亦豈可得至！

translations.literal: If we moved at once, we would collapse of ourselves like earth tumbling and tiles shattering—how could we even reach the north of the river!
translations.idiomatic: If we fled now, everything would fall apart—we could not even reach the north bank!

sentences.zh: 設令得至，不過延日月耳。

translations.literal: Supposing we could reach it, we would merely prolong days and months, that is all.
translations.idiomatic: Even if we got there, we would only buy a little time.

sentences.zh: 今兵士雖少，自足一戰。

translations.literal: Though our soldiers are few today, they are sufficient for one battle.
translations.idiomatic: We have few men, but enough for one fight.

sentences.zh: 若其克濟，則臣主同休；

translations.literal: If we succeed in overcoming them, then minister and lord share good fortune together;
translations.idiomatic: If we win, ruler and minister alike will prosper;

sentences.zh: 苟厄運必至，我當橫屍廟門，遂其由來以身許國之志，不能竄伏草間苟求存活也。

translations.literal: If ill fortune must come, I shall lie slain across the temple gate, fulfilling my long-held resolve to devote my body to the state—I cannot skulk in the grass merely to cling to life.
translations.idiomatic: If fate turns against us, I shall die across the temple gate, keeping the vow I have always held to give my life for the state. I will not hide in the weeds merely to survive.

sentences.zh: 我計決矣，卿勿復言！」

translations.literal: My decision is made; do not speak again!"
translations.idiomatic: My mind is made up—say no more!"

sentences.zh: 昶恚其言不行，且以為必敗，因請死。

translations.literal: Chang resented that his words were not followed and, holding that defeat was certain, thereupon asked to die.
translations.idiomatic: Chang was angry that Yu would not listen, convinced defeat was inevitable, and asked to die.

sentences.zh: 裕怒曰：「卿且申一戰，死復何晚！」

translations.literal: Yu angrily said, "You may first join one battle—what is late about dying then!"
translations.idiomatic: Yu snapped, "Fight one battle first—what hurry is there to die!"

sentences.zh: 昶知裕終不用其言，乃抗表自陳曰：「臣裕北討，眾並不同，唯臣贊裕行計，致使強賊乘間，社稷危逼，臣之罪也。

translations.literal: Chang knew Yu would never adopt his counsel, and so submitted a memorial declaring himself: "When subject Yu marched north to attack, all differed; only I approved Yu's plan. This enabled strong rebels to seize an opening; the altars of state are pressed in peril—it is my crime.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that Yu would never heed him, Chang submitted a formal memorial: "When Yu marched north, none agreed but I alone urged the campaign. That let a powerful enemy strike at our weakness and put the realm in peril—the fault is mine.

sentences.zh: 謹引咎以謝天下！」

translations.literal: I respectfully take blame to apologize to all under Heaven!"
translations.idiomatic: I accept full blame before the empire!"

sentences.zh: 封表畢，仰藥而死。

translations.literal: Having sealed the memorial, he drank poison and died.
translations.idiomatic: When he had sealed it, he took poison and died.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，盧循至淮口，中外戒嚴。

translations.literal: On yichou, Lu Xun reached the Huai River mouth; court and countryside were placed on alert.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou, Lu Xun reached the mouth of the Huai; the capital and provinces went on full alert.

sentences.zh: 琅邪王德文都督宮城諸軍事，屯中堂皇，劉裕屯石頭，諸將各有屯守。

translations.literal: Prince of Langya Dewen took supreme command of all forces in the palace city and encamped in the central hall; Liu Yu encamped at Shitou; the various generals each had their garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Langya Dewen took command of the palace defenses and encamped in the central hall; Liu Yu held Shitou; each general occupied his assigned post.

sentences.zh: 裕子義隆始四歲，裕使咨議參軍劉粹輔之，鎮京口。

translations.literal: Yu's son Yilong was only four years old; Yu sent Consulting Aide Liu Cui to assist him and garrisoned him at Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: Yu's son Yilong was only four; Yu sent consulting aide Liu Cui to assist him and posted them at Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 粹，毅之族弟也。

translations.literal: Cui was a clansman younger cousin of Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Cui was a younger kinsman of Liu Yi.

sentences.zh: 裕見民臨水望賊，怪之，以問參軍張劭，劭曰：「若節鉞未反，民奔散之不暇，亦何能觀望？

translations.literal: Yu saw the people lining the water to watch the rebels and thought it strange; he asked aide Zhang Shao. Shao said, "If the commander's credentials had not returned, the people would have fled scattering with no spare moment—how could they look on?
translations.idiomatic: Yu saw people lining the riverbank to watch the enemy and asked aide Zhang Shao about it. Shao said, "If you had not yet returned in triumph, they would have been fleeing for their lives—who could stand and watch?

sentences.zh: 今當無復恐耳。

translations.literal: Now they ought to have no fear again, that is all.
translations.idiomatic: Now they know there is nothing left to fear.

sentences.zh: 賊若於新亭直進，其鋒不可當，宜且迴避，勝負之事未可量也；

translations.literal: If the rebels pressed straight ahead at Xinting, their sharp edge could not be withstood; we should for the time being avoid them—the matter of victory or defeat could not yet be measured;
translations.idiomatic: If they drove straight on from Xinting, their momentum would be unstoppable; we would have to pull back, and the outcome would be uncertain;

sentences.zh: 若回泊西岸，此成禽耳。」

translations.literal: If they turned back and anchored on the west bank, these would simply become prisoners caught."
translations.idiomatic: If they withdraw and moor on the west bank, they are as good as captured."

sentences.zh: 徐道覆請於新亭至白石焚舟而上，數道攻裕。

translations.literal: Xu Daofu asked to burn the boats at Xinting and proceed up to Baishi, attacking Yu on several routes.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Daofu urged burning the boats from Xinting to Baishi and advancing overland to strike Yu on several fronts.

sentences.zh: 循欲以萬全為計，謂道覆曰：「大軍未至，孟昶便望風自裁；

translations.literal: Xun wished to plan for absolute safety and said to Daofu, "The great army has not yet arrived, yet Meng Chang has already cut himself down at the mere rumor of our approach;
translations.idiomatic: Xun favored the safe course and told Daofu, "Our main force has not even arrived, yet Meng Chang has already killed himself at the rumor of our coming;

sentences.zh: 以大勢言之，自當計日潰亂。

translations.literal: Speaking in terms of the great situation, they should naturally fall apart within numbered days.
translations.idiomatic: Judging by the overall situation, they should collapse within days.

sentences.zh: 今決勝負於一朝，乾沒求利，既非必克之道，且殺傷士卒，不如按兵待之。」

translations.literal: Now to decide victory and defeat in a single morning, recklessly plunging to seek profit, is neither a way sure to overcome them nor only wounds and kills soldiers—better to hold the army and wait."
translations.idiomatic: To stake everything on one day's battle, gambling for gain when victory is uncertain, will only waste lives. Better to hold our troops and wait."

sentences.zh: 道覆以循多疑少決，乃歎曰：「我終為盧公所誤，事必無成；

translations.literal: Daofu, because Xun was overly suspicious and short on resolve, sighed and said, "In the end I am misled by Lord Lu—the undertaking is sure not to succeed;
translations.idiomatic: Daofu thought Xun too hesitant and mistrustful, and sighed, "Lu has ruined me—this venture is doomed;

sentences.zh: 使我得為英雄驅馳，天下不足定也。」

translations.literal: If I could drive as a hero drives, all under Heaven would not be hard to settle."
translations.idiomatic: Given a free hand, I could pacify the empire without difficulty."

sentences.zh: 裕登石頭城望循軍，初見引向新亭，顧左右失色；

translations.literal: Yu climbed Shitou city wall to look on Xun's army; at first he saw them heading toward Xinting and turned to those at his side, his color lost;
translations.idiomatic: Yu climbed the walls of Shitou to watch Xun's army. When he first saw them heading for Xinting, he turned pale.

sentences.zh: 既而回泊蔡洲，乃悅。

translations.literal: Presently they turned back and anchored at Caizhou, and then he was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: When they withdrew and anchored at Caizhou, he was relieved.

sentences.zh: 於是眾軍轉集。

translations.literal: Thereupon the various armies gathered in turn.
translations.idiomatic: All the armies now converged.

sentences.zh: 裕恐循侵軼，用虞丘進計，伐樹柵石頭淮口，修治越城，築查浦、藥園、廷尉三壘，皆以兵守之。

translations.literal: Yu, fearing Xun might raid and sweep across, adopted Yuqiu Jin's plan: felled trees to palisade Shitou at the Huai mouth, repaired Yue city, and built three strongholds at Zhapu, Yaoyuan, and Tingwei, all garrisoned with troops.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Xun might break through, Yu took Yuqiu Jin's advice: timber palisades at Shitou by the Huai, repairs to Yue city, and new fortifications at Zhapu, Yaoyuan, and Tingwei—all manned.

sentences.zh: 劉毅經涉蠻、晉，僅能自免，從者饑疲，死亡什七八。

translations.literal: Liu Yi passed through Miao and Jin lands, barely escaping with his life; those who followed were hungry and exhausted, seven or eight in ten dying.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi had crossed through tribal and Jin territory and barely escaped alive; his men were starving and exhausted, and seven or eight in ten were dead.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，至建康，待罪。

translations.literal: On bingyin, he reached Jiankang and awaited punishment.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin he reached Jiankang to await judgment.

sentences.zh: 裕慰勉之，使知中外留事。

translations.literal: Yu comforted and encouraged him and had him oversee affairs left behind in court and countryside.
translations.idiomatic: Yu reassured him and put him in charge of affairs at the capital.

sentences.zh: 毅乞自貶，詔降為後將軍。

translations.literal: Yi asked to demote himself; an edict reduced him to Rear General.
translations.idiomatic: Yi asked to be demoted; the court reduced him to Rear General.

sentences.zh: 魏長孫嵩至漠北而還，柔然追圍之於牛川。

translations.literal: Wei officer Changsun Song reached the far northern desert and returned; Rouran pursued and besieged him at Niuchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's Changsun Song marched to the northern steppe and back; the Rouran surrounded him at Niuchuan.

sentences.zh: 壬申，魏主嗣北擊柔然。

translations.literal: On renshen, Wei ruler Si struck north against Rouran.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen Emperor Si of Wei marched north against the Rouran.

sentences.zh: 柔然可汗社侖聞之，遁走，道死；

translations.literal: Rouran khan Shelun heard of it, fled, and died on the road;
translations.idiomatic: When Rouran khan Shelun heard, he fled and died on the way;

sentences.zh: 其子度拔尚幼，部眾立社侖弟斛律，號藹苦蓋可汗。

translations.literal: His son Dubo was still young; the tribesmen installed Shelun's younger brother Hulu, styled him Khan Aikugai.
translations.idiomatic: His son Dubo was still a child; the tribes raised Shelun's brother Hulu as Khan Aikugai.

sentences.zh: 嗣引兵還參合陂。

translations.literal: Si led his army back to Canhepi.
translations.idiomatic: Si withdrew to Canhepi.

sentences.zh: 盧循伏兵南岸，使老弱乘舟向白石，聲言悉眾自白石步上。

translations.literal: Lu Xun hid troops on the south bank, sent the old and weak in boats toward Baishi, and proclaimed aloud that the whole force would march up from Baishi on foot.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xun hid troops on the south bank while sending the old and weak by boat toward Baishi, claiming his entire army would land at Baishi and march inland.

sentences.zh: 劉裕留參軍沈林子、徐赤特戍南岸，斷查浦，戒今堅守勿動；

translations.literal: Liu Yu left aides Shen Linzi and Xu Chite to garrison the south bank, cut off Zhapu, and ordered them to hold firm and not move;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu left aides Shen Linzi and Xu Chite on the south bank to hold Zhapu and ordered them not to stir;

sentences.zh: 裕及劉毅、諸葛長民北出拒之。

translations.literal: Yu together with Liu Yi and Zhuge Changmin went north to resist them.
translations.idiomatic: Yu marched north with Liu Yi and Zhuge Changmin to meet the enemy.

sentences.zh: 林子曰：「妖賊此言，未必有實，宜深為之防。」

translations.literal: Linzi said, "This talk of the demonic rebels is not necessarily true; we should guard deeply against it."
translations.idiomatic: Linzi said, "The enemy's story may be a bluff—we must guard against it carefully."

sentences.zh: 裕曰：「石頭城險，且淮柵甚固，留卿在後，足以守之。」

translations.literal: Yu said, "Shitou city is perilous terrain, and the Huai palisade is very solid; leaving you behind is sufficient to hold it."
translations.idiomatic: Yu replied, "Shitou is strong and the Huai defenses are solid. With you in the rear, it is secure enough."

sentences.zh: 林子，穆夫之子也。

translations.literal: Linzi was the son of Mufu.
translations.idiomatic: Linzi was the son of Shen Mufu.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，盧循焚查浦，進至張侯橋。

translations.literal: On gengchen, Lu Xun burned Zhapu and advanced to Zhanghou Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen Lu Xun burned Zhapu and advanced to Zhanghou Bridge.

sentences.zh: 徐赤特將擊之，林子曰：「賊聲往白石而屢來挑戰，其情可知。

translations.literal: Xu Chite was about to strike them; Linzi said, "The rebels proclaim they are going to Baishi yet repeatedly come to challenge battle—their intent can be known.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Chite wanted to attack; Linzi said, "They claim to be bound for Baishi yet keep provoking us—their plan is obvious.

sentences.zh: 吾眾寡不敵，不如守險以待大軍。」

translations.literal: Our numbers, few against many, cannot match them; better to hold perilous ground and await the great army."
translations.idiomatic: We are outnumbered; better to hold our ground and wait for the main force."

sentences.zh: 赤特不從。

translations.literal: Chite did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Chite would not listen.

sentences.zh: 遂出戰，伏兵發，赤特大敗，單舸奔淮北。

translations.literal: Thereupon he went out to battle; ambush troops sprang up; Chite was greatly defeated and fled in a single boat to the north of the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: He went out to fight; the ambush struck and Chite was routed, escaping alone in a boat north of the Huai.

sentences.zh: 林子及將軍劉鐘據柵力戰，朱齡石救之，賊乃退。

translations.literal: Linzi and General Liu Zhong held the palisade and fought with all their strength; Zhu Lingshi rescued them, and the rebels then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Linzi and General Liu Zhong held the palisade; Zhu Lingshi came to their aid and the enemy withdrew.

sentences.zh: 循引精兵大上，至丹陽郡。

translations.literal: Xun led elite troops in a great landing and reached Danyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Xun landed with elite troops and pushed into Danyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 裕帥諸軍馳還石頭，斬徐赤特，解甲。

translations.literal: Yu led the various armies racing back to Shitou, executed Xu Chite, and laid aside armor.
translations.idiomatic: Yu raced back to Shitou with his army, executed Xu Chite, and rested his troops.

sentences.zh: 久之，乃出陳於南塘。

translations.literal: After a long while, he then deployed ranks at Nantang.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he formed battle lines at Nantang.

sentences.zh: 六月，以劉裕為太尉、中書監、加黃鉞；

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Liu Yu was made Grand Commandant, Director of the Secretariat, and given the yellow axe;
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Liu Yu was appointed Grand Commandant and Director of the Secretariat and granted the ceremonial axe;

sentences.zh: 裕受黃鉞，餘固辭。

translations.literal: Yu accepted the yellow axe but firmly declined the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Yu accepted the axe but declined the other honors.

sentences.zh: 以車騎中軍司馬庾悅為江州刺史。

translations.literal: Chariots-and-Cavalry Central Army Major Yu Yue was made Governor of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yue was appointed governor of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 悅，准之子也。

translations.literal: Yue was the son of Zhun.
translations.idiomatic: Yue was the son of Yu Zhun.

sentences.zh: 司馬國璠及弟叔璠、叔道奔秦。

translations.literal: Sima Guofan and his younger brothers Shufan and Shudao fled to Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Guofan and his brothers Shufan and Shudao fled to Later Qin.

sentences.zh: 秦王興曰：「劉裕方誅桓玄，輔晉室，卿何為來？」

translations.literal: Qin king Xing said, "Liu Yu has just executed Huan Xuan and assists the Jin house—why have you come?"
translations.idiomatic: King Xing of Qin asked, "Liu Yu has just overthrown Huan Xuan and supports the Jin court—why have you come?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「裕削弱王室，臣宗族有自修立者，裕輒除之。

translations.literal: They replied, "Yu weakens the royal house; whenever members of my clan sought to restore themselves, Yu would always remove them.
translations.idiomatic: They answered, "Yu is stripping the imperial house of power. Whenever one of our clan tried to rebuild our position, Yu destroyed him.

sentences.zh: 方為國患，甚於桓玄耳。」

translations.literal: He is becoming a national calamity, worse than Huan Xuan, that is all."
translations.idiomatic: He is a greater threat to the state than Huan Xuan ever was."

sentences.zh: 興以國璠為揚州刺史，叔道為交州刺史。

translations.literal: Xing made Guofan Governor of Yangzhou and Shudao Governor of Jiaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xing made Guofan governor of Yangzhou and Shudao governor of Jiaozhou.

sentences.zh: 盧循寇掠諸縣無所得，謂徐道覆曰：「師老矣，不如還尋陽，並力取荊州，據天下三分之二，徐更與建康爭衡耳。」

translations.literal: Lu Xun raided and plundered the various counties without gain and said to Xu Daofu, "The army is weary; better to return to Xunyang, combine strength to take Jingzhou, hold two-thirds of all under Heaven, and then slowly contend with Jiankang again, that is all."
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xun had looted the countryside without success and told Xu Daofu, "Our troops are exhausted. We should return to Xunyang, seize Jingzhou together, hold two-thirds of the empire, and then compete with Jiankang at leisure."

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，庚申，循自蔡洲南還尋陽，留其黨范崇民將五千人據南陵。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on gengshen, Xun returned south from Caizhou to Xunyang, leaving his partisan Fan Chongmin with five thousand men to hold Nanling.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, on gengshen, Xun withdrew south from Caizhou to Xunyang, leaving Fan Chongmin with five thousand men at Nanling.

sentences.zh: 甲子，裕使輔國將軍王仲德、廣川太守劉鐘、河間內史蘭陵蒯恩、中軍咨議參軍孟懷玉等帥眾追循。

translations.literal: On jiazi, Yu sent Auxiliary State General Wang Zhongde, Governor of Guangchuan Liu Zhong, Interior Secretary of Hejian Lanling Kuai En, Central Army Consulting Aide Meng Huaiyu, and others to lead troops in pursuit of Xun.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi Yu sent Wang Zhongde, Liu Zhong, Kuai En, Meng Huaiyu, and others in pursuit of Xun.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，魏主嗣還平城。

translations.literal: On yichou, Wei ruler Si returned to Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou Emperor Si of Wei returned to Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 西秦王乾歸討越質屈機等十餘部，降其眾二萬五千，徙於苑川。

translations.literal: Western Qin king Qiangui attacked the Yuezhi Quji and more than ten other tribes, received the surrender of twenty-five thousand of their followers, and moved them to Yuanchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Qiangui of Western Qin subdued more than ten tribes including the Yuezhi Quji, accepted the surrender of twenty-five thousand warriors, and resettled them at Yuanchuan.

sentences.zh: 八月，乾歸復都苑川。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Qiangui again made Yuanchuan his capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Qiangui moved his capital back to Yuanchuan.

sentences.zh: 沮渠蒙遜伐西涼，敗西涼世子歆於馬廟，禽其將朱元虎而還。

translations.literal: Juqu Mengxun attacked Western Liang, defeated Western Liang heir Xin at Mabiao, captured his general Zhu Yuanhu, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Juqu Mengxun attacked Western Liang, defeated heir Xin at Mabiao, captured General Zhu Yuanhu, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 涼公暠以銀二千斤、金二千兩贖元虎；

translations.literal: Liang lord Gao ransomed Yuanhu with two thousand jin of silver and two thousand liang of gold;
translations.idiomatic: Lord Gao of Liang paid two thousand jin of silver and two thousand liang of gold to ransom Yuanhu;

sentences.zh: 蒙遜歸之，遂與暠結盟而還。

translations.literal: Mengxun returned him and thereupon allied with Gao by oath and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun released him, made peace with Gao, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 劉裕還東府，大治水軍，遣建威將軍會稽孫處、振武將軍沈田子帥眾三千自海道襲番禺。

translations.literal: Liu Yu returned to the Eastern Headquarters, greatly built up the navy, and sent Establishing Might General Sun Chu of Kuaiji and Stirring Martial General Shen Tianzi to lead three thousand men by sea route to raid Panyu.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu returned to his Eastern Headquarters and rebuilt the navy, sending Sun Chu and Shen Tianzi with three thousand men by sea to strike Panyu.

sentences.zh: 田子，林子之兄也。

translations.literal: Tianzi was the elder brother of Linzi.
translations.idiomatic: Tianzi was Shen Linzi's elder brother.

sentences.zh: 眾皆以為「海道艱遠，必至為難，且分撤見力，非目前之急。」

translations.literal: All thought, "The sea route is arduous and far; trouble is sure to come, and moreover it divides and scatters present strength—not an urgent matter of the moment."
translations.idiomatic: Many objected that the sea route was long and risky, that it would divide their forces, and that it was not the immediate priority."

sentences.zh: 裕不從，敕處曰：「大軍十二月之交必破妖虜，卿至時，先傾其巢窟，使彼走無所歸也。」

translations.literal: Yu did not follow; he instructed Chu, "The great army at the turn of the twelfth month is sure to smash the demonic rebels; when you arrive, first overturn their nest so that when they flee they have nowhere to return."
translations.idiomatic: Yu overruled them and told Chu, "By mid-December the main army will break the enemy. Your task is to destroy their base so they have nowhere to flee."

sentences.zh: 譙縱遣侍中譙良等入見於秦，請兵以伐晉。

translations.literal: Qiao Zong sent Palace Attendant Qiao Liang and others to enter and be received by Qin, requesting troops to attack Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao Zong sent Qiao Liang and others to Qin to ask for troops against Jin.

sentences.zh: 縱以桓謙為荊州刺史，譙道福為梁州刺史，帥眾二萬寇荊州；

translations.literal: Zong made Huan Qian Governor of Jingzhou and Qiao Daofu Governor of Liangzhou, leading twenty thousand men to raid Jingzhou;
translations.idiomatic: Zong appointed Huan Qian governor of Jingzhou and Qiao Daofu governor of Liangzhou and invaded with twenty thousand men;

sentences.zh: 秦王興遣前將軍苟林帥騎兵會之。

translations.literal: Qin king Xing sent Forward General Gou Lin to lead cavalry to join them.
translations.idiomatic: King Xing sent Forward General Gou Lin with cavalry to join them.

sentences.zh: 江陵自盧循東下，不得建康之問，群盜互起。

translations.literal: From the time Lu Xun came east downriver, Jiangling received no news from Jiankang; bandits rose one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Since Lu Xun marched east, Jiangling had heard nothing from Jiankang and banditry had erupted everywhere.

sentences.zh: 荊州刺史劉道規遣司馬王鎮之帥天門太守檀道濟、廣武將軍彭城到彥之入援建康。

translations.literal: Jingzhou Governor Liu Daogui sent Major Wang Zhenzhi to lead Tainmen Governor Tan Daoji, Broad Martial General Pengcheng Dao Yanzhi, and others to enter and relieve Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Liu Daogui of Jingzhou sent Wang Zhenzhi with Tan Daoji and Dao Yanzhi toward Jiankang to reinforce the capital.

sentences.zh: 道濟，祗之弟也。

translations.literal: Daoji was the younger brother of Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Daoji was the younger brother of Tan Zhi.

sentences.zh: 鎮之至尋陽，為苟林所破。

translations.literal: When Zhenzhi reached Xunyang, he was defeated by Gou Lin.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzhi reached Xunyang and was defeated by Gou Lin.

sentences.zh: 盧循聞之，以林為南蠻校尉，分兵配之，使乘勝伐江陵，聲言徐道覆已克建康。

translations.literal: Lu Xun heard of it, made Lin Protector-General of Southern Man, allotted troops to him, and had him exploit victory to attack Jiangling, proclaiming aloud that Xu Daofu had already taken Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xun heard the news, made Gou Lin Protector-General of the Southern Barbarians, gave him troops, and sent him on to Jiangling while spreading word that Xu Daofu had already taken Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 桓謙於道召募義舊，民投之者二萬人。

translations.literal: Huan Qian along the route recruited former loyalists; people who joined him numbered twenty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Qian recruited old Huan loyalists along the way and gathered twenty thousand men.

sentences.zh: 謙屯枝江，林屯江津，二寇交逼，江陵士民多懷異心。

translations.literal: Qian encamped at Zhijiang, Lin at Jiangjin; the two invaders pressed from both sides, and many of Jiangling's gentry and commoners harbored divided hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Qian camped at Zhijiang and Lin at Jiangjin; with enemies pressing from two sides, many in Jiangling were ready to turn.

sentences.zh: 道規乃會將士告之曰：「桓謙今在近道，聞諸長者頗有去就之計，吾東來文武足以濟事，若欲去者，本不相禁。」

translations.literal: Daogui thereupon assembled officers and soldiers and told them, "Huan Qian is now on the near road; I hear that many elders have plans to stay or go—our civil and military who came east are sufficient to accomplish the task; if any wish to leave, I originally do not forbid it."
translations.idiomatic: Daogui gathered his officers and men and said, "Huan Qian is close at hand. I hear some of you elders are thinking of leaving. Our force from the east is enough to see this through. If anyone wishes to go, I will not stop you."

sentences.zh: 因夜開城門，達曉不閉。

translations.literal: Thereupon in the night he opened the city gates and until dawn did not close them.
translations.idiomatic: That night he opened the city gates and left them open until dawn.

sentences.zh: 眾鹹憚服，莫有去者。

translations.literal: The masses all feared and submitted; none left.
translations.idiomatic: The people were awed into loyalty; no one left.

sentences.zh: 雍州刺史魯宗之帥眾數千自襄陽赴江陵。

translations.literal: Yongzhou Governor Lu Zongzhi led several thousand men from Xiangyang to hasten to Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zongzhi, governor of Yongzhou, marched from Xiangyang with several thousand men to relieve Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 或謂宗之情未可測，道規單馬迎之，宗之感悅。

translations.literal: Some said Zongzhi's intentions could not yet be measured; Daogui went alone on horseback to meet him, and Zongzhi was moved and pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Some doubted Zongzhi's loyalty, but Daogui rode out alone to meet him and won his trust.

sentences.zh: 道規使宗之居守，委以腹心，自帥諸軍攻謙。

translations.literal: Daogui had Zongzhi remain to garrison, entrusted him as innermost confidant, and himself led the various armies to attack Qian.
translations.idiomatic: Daogui put Zongzhi in charge of the defense and treated him as a trusted ally, then marched out to attack Qian.

sentences.zh: 諸將佐皆曰：「今遠出討謙，其勝難必。

translations.literal: The various generals and aides all said, "Now going far out to attack Qian, victory is hard to be sure of.
translations.idiomatic: His officers said, "If we march out to fight Qian, victory is uncertain.

sentences.zh: 苟林近在江津，伺人動靜，若來攻城，宗之未必能固；

translations.literal: Gou Lin is close at Jiangjin, watching people's movements; if he comes to attack the city, Zongzhi may not necessarily be able to hold firm;
translations.idiomatic: Gou Lin is nearby at Jiangjin watching for an opening. If he attacks the city, Zongzhi may not hold;

sentences.zh: 脫有蹉跌，大事去矣。」

translations.literal: If by mischance there is a stumble, the great affair is lost."
translations.idiomatic: One slip and all is lost."

sentences.zh: 道規曰：「苟林愚懦，無他奇計，以吾去未遠，必不敢向城。

translations.literal: Daogui said, "Gou Lin is foolish and timid, with no other clever plan; because we have not gone far, he surely dare not turn toward the city.
translations.idiomatic: Daogui replied, "Gou Lin is slow and timid and has no tricks. We won't be gone long enough for him to dare attack the city.

sentences.zh: 吾今取謙，往至便克；

translations.literal: Now I take Qian—once we go, we shall at once overcome him;
translations.idiomatic: I will take Qian quickly—once we strike, he will fall;

sentences.zh: 沈疑之間，已自還返。

translations.literal: In the interval of hesitation and doubt, I shall already have returned myself.
translations.idiomatic: By the time Gou Lin decides to move, I will already be back.

sentences.zh: 謙敗則林破膽。

translations.literal: When Qian is defeated, Lin will lose heart.
translations.idiomatic: Defeat Qian, and Gou Lin will lose his nerve.

sentences.zh: 豈暇得來！

translations.literal: How could he have leisure to come!
translations.idiomatic: He will not have time to come!

sentences.zh: 且宗之獨守，何為不支數日！」

translations.literal: Moreover, Zongzhi alone holding the defense—why would he not hold out for several days!"
translations.idiomatic: Besides, Zongzhi can hold the city alone for days!"

sentences.zh: 乃馳往攻謙，水陸齊進。

translations.literal: Then he galloped off to attack Qian, advancing together by water and land.
translations.idiomatic: With that, he rode out to attack Qian by land and water at once.

sentences.zh: 謙等大陳舟師，兼以步騎，戰於枝江。

translations.literal: Qian and the others greatly arrayed the fleet, together with infantry and cavalry, and fought at Zhijiang.
translations.idiomatic: Qian massed his fleet along with infantry and cavalry and gave battle at Zhijiang.

sentences.zh: 檀道濟先進陷陳，謙等大敗。

translations.literal: Tan Daoji advanced first and broke the formation; Qian and the others were greatly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Daoji led the charge and broke their lines; Qian's army was routed.

sentences.zh: 謙單舸奔苟林，道規追斬之。

translations.literal: Qian in a single boat fled to Gou Lin; Daogui pursued and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Qian fled alone in a boat toward Gou Lin, but Daogui caught up and killed him.

sentences.zh: 還，至湧口，討林，林走，道規遣咨議參軍臨淮劉遵帥眾追之。

translations.literal: Returning, arriving at Yongkou, he attacked Lin; Lin fled. Daogui sent Advisory Army Attendant Liu Zun of Linhuai to lead the host in pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: On the return march Daogui reached Yongkou and attacked Gou Lin, who fled. Daogui sent Liu Zun, staff officer of Linhuai, in pursuit with his troops.

sentences.zh: 初，謙至枝江，江陵士民皆與謙書。

translations.literal: Initially, when Qian reached Zhijiang, the gentry and commoners of Jiangling all sent letters to Qian.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Qian reached Zhijiang, many people in Jiangling had written to him.

sentences.zh: 言城內虛實，欲為內應；

translations.literal: Stating the emptiness and fullness within the city, wishing to serve as internal collaborators;
translations.idiomatic: reporting on conditions inside the city and offering to rise up within the walls;

sentences.zh: 至是檢得之，道規悉焚不視，眾於是大安。

translations.literal: At this time they were found upon inspection; Daogui burned them all without reading, and the masses thereupon greatly settled.
translations.idiomatic: When the letters were discovered, Daogui burned them unread, and the people were greatly reassured.

sentences.zh: 江州刺史庾悅以鄱陽太守虞丘進為前驅，屢破盧循兵，進據豫章，絕循糧道。

translations.literal: Jiangzhou Governor Yu Yue made Poyang Prefect Yu Qiu Jin vanguard; repeatedly defeated Lu Xun's troops, advanced and occupied Yuzhang, cutting off Xun's grain route.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yue, governor of Jiangzhou, sent Poyang prefect Yu Qiu Jin ahead as vanguard. Jin repeatedly defeated Lu Xun's forces, seized Yuzhang, and severed Xun's supply lines.

sentences.zh: 九月，劉遵斬苟林於巴陵。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Liu Zun beheaded Gou Lin at Baling.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Liu Zun killed Gou Lin at Baling.

sentences.zh: 桓石綏因循入寇，起兵洛口，自號荊州刺史，征陽令王天恩自號梁州刺史，襲據西城。

translations.literal: Huan Shisui, taking advantage of Lu Xun's invasion, raised troops at Luokou and styled himself Governor of Jingzhou; Zhengyang Magistrate Wang Tian'en styled himself Governor of Liangzhou and by surprise seized Xicheng.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Shisui exploited Lu Xun's invasion to rebel at Luokou, proclaiming himself governor of Jingzhou. Wang Tian'en, magistrate of Zhengyang, proclaimed himself governor of Liangzhou and seized Xicheng by surprise.

sentences.zh: 梁州刺史傅詔遣其子魏興太守弘之討石綏等，皆斬之，桓氏遂滅。

translations.literal: Liangzhou Governor Fu Shao sent his son Weixing Prefect Hongzhi to attack Shisui and the others; all were beheaded, and the Huan clan was thereupon extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Shao, governor of Liangzhou, sent his son Fu Hongzhi, prefect of Weixing, against Shisui and his followers. All were executed, and the Huan line was wiped out.

sentences.zh: 韶，暢之孫也。

translations.literal: Shao was Chang's grandson.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Shao was a grandson of Fu Chang.

sentences.zh: 西秦王乾歸攻秦略陽、南安、隴西諸郡，皆克之，徙民二萬五千戶於苑川及枹罕。

translations.literal: Western Qin King Qiangui attacked Qin's Lueyang, Nan'an, Longxi and various commanderies; all were taken. He moved twenty-five thousand households of people to Yuanchuan and Fuhan.
translations.idiomatic: Qifu Gangui, king of Western Qin, attacked the Qin commanderies of Lueyang, Nan'an, and Longxi and took them all. He relocated twenty-five thousand households to Yuanchuan and Fuhan.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，葬魏主珪於盛樂金陵，謚曰宣武，廟號烈祖。

translations.literal: On jia-yin, the Wei ruler Gui was buried at Shengle Jinling; posthumous title Xuanwu, temple name Liezu.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jia-yin, Wei emperor Tuoba Gui was buried at the Jinling tombs at Shengle, with the posthumous name Emperor Xuanwu and temple name Liezu.

sentences.zh: 劉毅固求追討盧循，長史王誕密言於劉裕曰：「毅既喪敗，不宜復使立功。」

translations.literal: Liu Yi steadfastly requested to pursue and attack Lu Xun. Chief Clerk Wang Dan secretly spoke to Liu Yu, saying, "Yi having already suffered defeat, it is not fitting to let him win merit again."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi pressed Liu Yu to let him pursue Lu Xun. Chief clerk Wang Dan secretly advised Liu Yu, "Yi has already been humiliated in defeat; you should not give him another chance to win glory."

sentences.zh: 裕從之。

translations.literal: Yu followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu agreed.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，裕帥兗州刺史劉籓、寧朔將軍檀韶、冠軍將軍劉敬宣等南擊盧循，以劉毅監太尉留府，後事皆委焉。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, Yu led Yanzhou Governor Liu Fan, Ningshuo General Tan Shao, Champion General Liu Jingxuan and others south to attack Lu Xun; he had Liu Yi oversee the Grand Commandant's remaining headquarters, and all later affairs were entrusted to him.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter Liu Yu marched south against Lu Xun at the head of Liu Fan, governor of Yanzhou, Tan Shao, and Liu Jingxuan. He left Liu Yi in charge of affairs at the capital as acting overseer of the Grand Commandant's office.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，裕發建康。

translations.literal: On gui-si, Yu departed from Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: On the day gui-si Liu Yu set out from Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 徐道覆帥眾三萬趣江陵，奄至破塚。
